papers.title: Toward sustainable agritourism: operational insights from organic farms engaged with tourism
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how integrating organic farming with agritourism can advance sustainable rural development. By examining organic farms engaged with tourism in South Korea through an ecotourism framework, it addresses the need to distinguish genuinely sustainable, ecologically grounded agritourism models from conventional, chemical-intensive practices. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes a qualitative case study approach combining in-depth interviews with operators of three organic farms and a content analysis of 38 organic farm tourism websites in South Korea. The analysis evaluates farm operations, visitor programming and rural community dynamics against core ecotourism principles, contextualized with recent agritourism literature. Findings Organic agritourism aligns closely with ecotourism by integrating low-impact farming with hands-on environmental education, biodiversity conservation and cultural preservation. Key findings highlight that tourism revenue reinforces organic land stewardship, small-scale operations foster meaningful socio-cultural and educational exchanges and participatory community collaboration enhances rural resilience and local circular economies. Five operational takeaways are identified: ecological conservation, active learning, socio-cultural sustainability, value-based economic viability and inclusive community participation. Originality/value This paper demonstrates that ecotourism serves as an effective guiding paradigm for agritourism on small-scale organic enterprises. It provides actionable operational and policy insights for agritourism operators, planners and government agencies seeking to establish replicable, value-based agritourism models that support environmental integrity, rural vitality and ethical visitor engagement.

papers.title: Parametric design of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V rhombic dodecahedron and Voronoi lattice structures for potential orthopedic applications
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate a unified parametric design framework for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-fabricated Ti-6Al-4V scaffolds and compares two architectural classes: a regular rhombic dodecahedron lattice and a stochastic Voronoi-based lattice, with emphasis on macrostructure and mechanical performance. Design/methodology/approach Scaffold geometries were parametrically defined within geometric and manufacturability constraints using open-source mathematical formulations. Specimens were manufactured by LPBF and characterized via gravimetric analysis, X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) and quasi-static compression testing. Findings Measured structural porosity ranged from ∼59 % to ∼80 %. For rhombic dodecahedron lattices, porosity decreased relative to STL models as unit-cell size decreased, with deviations of 7%–15 %. Voronoi scaffolds showed smaller deviations (−1.5% to 4%). Mechanical properties were strongly correlated with measured porosity. Rhombic dodecahedron structures exhibited Young’s modulus of 1.3–3.7 GPa and apparent yield strength of 41–154 MPa, exceeding those of Voronoi structures (0.9–2.6 GPa and 19–99 MPa, respectively). At fixed geometric parameters, mechanical properties varied approximately linearly with porosity. The governing structural factors differed by topology, with strut number dominating in regular lattices and strut thickness and organic factor governing in stochastic lattices. The results are limited to the investigated geometries and LPBF processing conditions. Fatigue, permeability, biological response and full-scale implant validation were outside the scope of this study. Originality/value The proposed framework enables a direct comparison of regular and stochastic Ti-6Al-4V scaffold architectures fabricated by LPBF and explicitly quantifies discrepancies between nominal CAD designs and as-built structures. By linking topology to manufacturability, porosity deviation and mechanical performance, the study identifies topology-dependent governing parameters: unit-cell size and strut thickness for regular lattices and strut thickness combined with organic factor for stochastic lattices. These results provide design guidelines that incorporate fabrication realities into the optimization of load-bearing orthopedic implants.

papers.title: Spectral arithmetic over orthomodular lattices
papers.abstract: Spectral families provide a representation of observables in quantum logic. This paper develops an addition operation for bounded spectral quantities over orthomodular lattices to examine the relation between familiar arithmetic behavior and lattice structure. The operation extends the established addition of bounded observables. Under this operation, bounded spectral quantities form an abelian group precisely when the lattice is Boolean. Conjugating the operation by spectral negation yields a dual sum, and equality of the primal and dual sums characterizes modularity. A modular non-Boolean example separates these two regimes concretely.

papers.title: At the Limit: Autonomous Vehicle Drifting under Generative Policies
papers.abstract: Autonomous drifting requires agile control despite tire-force saturation and highly nonlinear vehicle dynamics. We propose an online reinforcement learning method for flow policies that combines stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling for exploration with value-based policy optimization. This method supports both training from scratch and fine-tuning a policy pretrained on expert demonstrations. After training, control actions can be generated using either SDEs or ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Experiments on circular and eight-shaped drifting in an F1TENTH digital twin platform show that both training strategies can achieve effective real-time drift control, with tighter tracking, higher success rates, and better robustness under noisy conditions.

papers.title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for recommendation systems. However, their issued rankings require reliable instance-level uncertainty monitoring. In this scenario, comparing uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods becomes challenging because LLM rankers lack a standard item-classification head. Their scores may depend on option labels, prompts, generation procedures, and the available user and item evidence. Existing methods derive uncertainty from different sources and apply it at different stages of the recommendation process. Some methods evaluate an issued ranking, whereas others use uncertainty to change the ranking itself, making direct comparison difficult. Here we introduce a fixed-ranking benchmark which evaluates eight heterogeneous UQ signals as record-level monitors under a shared output contract. We evaluate these signals across four recommendation datasets and two LLM backbones under a shared fixed-ranking protocol. From the results, we draw three main observations. First, UQ method ordering changes across backbones even on the same reference instances. Second, ranking-aligned Top10Mass provides the strongest scalar Error@10 detection in several evaluation conditions, reflecting effective cutoff-aligned monitoring, while its advantage narrows for popularity-tail targets. Third, scalar UQ signals are weak at identifying which control has the larger clipped NDCG@10 difference, whereas source-specific signals, including Perturbation Rank Instability and simple listwise distances, provide stronger paired-control agreement, reflecting their sensitivity to the two controlled evidence sources. These findings motivate us to evaluate ranking-failure detection, robustness across recommendation conditions, and responses to controlled evidence changes as distinct properties of UQ.

papers.title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective
papers.abstract: AI-native radio access network (RAN) control involves interdependent decisions across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. Understanding how AI and conventional methods can jointly support these decisions requires a common basis for comparing their functional roles. This survey introduces a technique-agnostic taxonomy of RAN decision-making organized around four complementary capabilities: Representation and Reasoning, Prediction and Simulation, Adaptive Control, and Decision Synthesis. These capabilities are defined by their roles in the control process, independently of the techniques used to implement them. Through this perspective, we examine representative AI and model-based approaches, including foundation models, world models, reinforcement learning, and optimization. We then apply the taxonomy to representative RAN control solutions across slow, medium, fast, and cross-timescale applications to identify which capabilities they implement and how these capabilities are combined in hybrid AI systems. We also review datasets, benchmarks, simulators, digital twins, and experimental platforms according to their support for the decision-making process and reproducible evaluation. The review highlights a gap between the availability of resources for closed-loop experimentation and the standardization of tasks, metrics, and evaluation protocols needed for meaningful comparisons.Finally, we identify research directions for hybrid AI in AI-native RAN, including capability integration, multi-agent and cross-timescale coordination, constraint handling, and reproducible closed-loop evaluation. A curated list of surveyed works and evaluation resources is available at https://github.com/pegahani/Hybrid-AI-RAN-Survey.

papers.title: PAC-style Bounds on the Conditional Validity of Conformal Predictors
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction sets are guaranteed to be marginally valid over the attribute space, but local coverage can diverge from the user-defined target $1-α$. Constructing conditionally valid prediction sets with finite calibration data is impossible for a general data-generating distribution. We derive PAC-type probabilistic lower bounds on the input-conditional coverage of any conformal predictor, without assumptions on the data distribution. They are based on the Markov and Cantelli inequalities and adapt to both calibration-marginal and calibration-conditional setups. A tighter, model-dependent Cantelli bound depends on the variance of the conditional coverage and is estimable from data using a fully non-asymptotic Hoeffding argument. The results suggest conditional-coverage variance as a scalable and theoretically motivated empirical measure of conditional validity.

llm.why_not_core: It provides only theoretical coverage bounds for conformal predictors with no surrogate modeling, no FEA sampling efficiency, no constraint handling, and no implant or biomechanics application.

papers.title: DynaMimic: A Physics-Informed World Model for Humanoid Motion Tracking
papers.abstract: Whole-body motion tracking enables humanoid robots to reproduce diverse skills from human demonstrations. Existing model-free reinforcement learning methods either distill motion specialists into a single policy at the cost of performance or train a generalist policy directly using cluster-scale computation. SuperMimic reduces this computational cost through a differentiable world model that implicitly learns the physics shared across motions by predicting the next state from the current state and action. However, this implicit formulation may not fully capture the underlying physical processes. Errors around changes of support can accumulate over imagined rollouts used to train the tracking policy. To address this challenge, we introduce DynaMimic, a differentiable world model that explicitly incorporates shared physics into state prediction. Specifically, its network predicts a contact wrench at each candidate support link and a residual generalized force. DynaMimic then uses these predictions to compute the next state through closed-form Lagrangian forward dynamics. Across 60 full LAFAN1 motions, DynaMimic reduces mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) by 18.6% relative to SuperMimic. For terrain tracking, we give both methods the same local height maps. Relative to terrain-conditioned SuperMimic, DynaMimic reduces MPJPE by 14.9% on A3 Parkour (66.15 to 56.28~mm) and by 10.8% on GRAIL terrain clips (141.88 to 126.57~mm). On a real A3 humanoid, the learned policies can perform diverse skills, such as floor recovery, cartwheel and a box vault.

papers.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result. To recover this latent information from the noisy distribution in Shor order finding, we introduce a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method. We model how circuit errors shift, broaden, or weaken peaks in the output distribution. These models guide both the generation of synthetic training data and the design of a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain that attenuates or amplifies higher retained Fourier modes. We score each candidate order by averaging the correlations between its ideal distribution and the distributions measured in three circuit executions. The network adjusts these scores to guide the order estimate and determine the weights of a normalized mixture of the ideal distributions. On 1,351 simulated test cases for general modular exponentiation, held out by circuit configuration, exact order recovery rises from 19% to 34%, and the median Jensen-Shannon divergence from the ideal distribution falls by 50%, from 0.64 to 0.32. On 101 Mersenne rotation circuits executed across five IBM quantum processors, a separate model trained and calibrated in simulation increases the number of correct order estimates from 35 to 53. Algorithmic structure can remain recoverable even when noise makes it barely visible.

papers.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generalize once the DC configuration changes. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive EMT-level digital twin for DCs based on in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs). We formulate the EMT prediction task as a system identification problem under parametric uncertainty and develop a GPT-2-based framework that adapts to unseen DC configurations at inference time from a small set of EMT trajectory samples, without model retraining. The proposed framework is validated on three representative EMT scenarios and benchmarked against three baseline non-adaptive twins. Results demonstrate superior prediction accuracy, improved adaptability to unseen operating conditions, and substantial computational speedups compared to high-fidelity EMT simulation.

papers.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
papers.abstract: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.

papers.title: DED-Agent: An agentic AI method for autonomous thermal simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition
papers.abstract: In metal additive manufacturing (AM), process parameters set the local thermal history, which governs defects, microstructure and properties. Laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness, scan strategy and position combine into a design space of 10^4-10^6 conditions, which is beyond what human experts can map by hand with finite element (FE) thermal models: every model must be set up, meshed, solved and calibrated by an expert, and calibrating unknown heat-source parameters alone can take days to weeks. This paper presents DED-Agent, an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) method for autonomous simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition (L-DED). A supervisor agent coordinates three specialist agents that share a structured simulation specification and call open-source tools. An intent agent turns a plain-language request into a validated specification, a simulation agent builds, runs and checks an FE thermal model through physics-aware step-by-step reasoning, and a calibration agent identifies key heat-source parameters against experimental data (e.g., thermocouple data) using a high-order proper generalized decomposition (HOPGD) surrogate within a trust-region search. On five benchmark builds, from single-track walls to a multi-track band on a cylindrical tube, the agents built executable thermal models without manual intervention, with 4.1-9.1% error for the simple and medium builds. Within three calibration rounds, the error fell to 0.9-2.5%. The surrogate matched full FE to within 0.08-1.55% and shortened calibration by 5-13 times. Agentic AI can thus autonomously establish reliable, accurate simulation models for AM processes and accelerate the search for process parameters that control microstructure.

papers.title: Interactive Neural Computers
papers.abstract: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents. This is limiting when someone needs a different workflow, or an interface suited to hands-free use or a disability. We explore an overlooked alternative. Rather than training an agent to operate an existing computer, we train a generative model to be the computer, predicting each next screen from past screens and the user's mouse and keyboard actions. Treating a desktop as an interactive world model raises problems that natural-video world models largely avoid. Without a camera pose to index memory, the model must remember content that has left the screen without any geometric cues. Arithmetic in a terminal has to be exactly right, not merely plausible. Small interface text must also stay legible at interactive frame rates. Our Interactive Neural Computer is structured like a Neural Turing Machine and starts to address these problems with three modules trained end to end from pixels and actions. A surprise-gated slot memory, supervised by latent next-frame prediction (MEMORY-JEPA), stores what is off screen. An exploratory query bridge brings in the reasoning of a pretrained VLM, and a residual renderer predicts only the latent changes between frames. In long closed-loop rollouts, our model recalls occluded files in 64.2% of trials (chance is 33.3%), compared with at most 56.0% for recurrent and sliding-window baselines. It also raises terminal-text OCR accuracy from 1.3% to 50.1%. Finally, because the memory is explicit, it can be transplanted at test time to causally change what the model renders.

papers.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
papers.abstract: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates. We argue that existing Bayesian Deep Learning solutions, which are often restricted to a fixed model family, fail to capture the full epistemic uncertainty at practical LLM scales. This is because the error due to the bounded capacity of the model family remains invisible to disagreement among models supported by the prior. We relate this error to the well-known power-law scaling of LLM loss with model size. We then show that a second power law quantifies the shrinking disagreement within ensembles as model size increases. Its slower decay relative to the capacity law above suggests that ensembles capture a growing share of epistemic uncertainty and become more competitive as an axis for scaling, compared to a single larger model. Finally, a third power law quantifies the loss of ensemble diversity as members share a larger fraction of training before branching, and therefore identifies a further limitation, beyond the capacity error, for LoRA ensembles and optimization-based or second-order methods that approximate uncertainty around a single training solution. At a high level, these findings suggest diverse ensembles can be a promising axis, both for scaling and uncertainty quantification at larger scales.

papers.title: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Video world models for robots are increasingly conditioned on a simulated or rendered proxy of the scene, on the assumption that the video will show what the proxy shows. Testing this assumption requires a proxy whose state is explicit and can be perturbed. We present SimPWM (Simulator-as-Proxy World Model): given a calibrated camera, it represents, from the first frame alone, the robot by its 3D model and the objects the gripper may touch as 3D points; a rule-based simulator with no trained parameters moves them under the actions, and a video model renders the result. SimPWM returns the realistic video together with the simulated state. We then freeze the simulated objects while the arm moves as recorded and check whether the video still shows the object lifted. On DROID episodes from unseen setups, the answer differs for the arm and for the objects. With each of three base video models, the arm follows the proxy (robot IoU 0.75-0.78, against at most 0.69 for end-to-end models); rendering the robot alone already gives this. What the simulated objects add is the object state: against a robot-only proxy, they cut missed pick-ups from 54% to 38%, and the video follows them only with some base models: on rigid objects, freezing them lowers the lift rate of MiniMax-H3, fine-tuned on episodes whose simulation agrees with the real video, from 42% to 10%, but that of LTX-2.3, trained on the same episodes, only from 57% to 49%, as if it inferred the grasp from the arm motion; more than half of the remaining lifts of MiniMax-H3 are of cloth and rope, which the simulator carries rigidly. With any base model, the simulated state records what the simulation did; under perturbed actions, a video that disagrees with it reveals that the video ignores the simulated state.

papers.title: Learning World Models through Contrastive Identification of Actions
papers.abstract: Latent world models enable goal-directed planning from offline visual data, but prediction alone does not specify which action-related distinctions their representations should preserve. Inverse dynamics provides auxiliary supervision, yet squared-error action regression rewards additional information only through changes in the conditional action mean. We propose Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), which identifies the executed action among alternatives sampled from a history-conditioned behavior proposal. Comparing actions plausible in the same context targets information supplied by the next latent beyond history. Under exact behavior matching, we show that CIA can reward action information that leaves optimal inverse-regression error unchanged, and verify this distinction through a controlled learning example. CIA achieves higher planner-averaged mean success than the base world model and a regression inverse-dynamics baseline across five visual control benchmarks, without modifying the planner.

papers.title: MemAnchorWorld: A Sparse World Model with Horizon-Conditioned Memory Retrieval for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Sparse world models for 4D semantic occupancy forecasting represent scenes with a small set of evolving queries to efficiently predict future geometry and semantics for autonomous driving. However, existing sparse world models face a bottleneck in using historical temporal evidence for long-horizon forecasting. They rely on scene states to carry historical information implicitly, allowing errors to propagate and accumulate across successive forecasting steps and causing geometric and semantic deviations. To address this limitation, we present MemAnchorWorld, a sparse occupancy world model that explicitly retrieves relevant historical geometric and semantic evidence for 4D semantic occupancy forecasting. Inspired by the von Restorff effect, we introduce a forecast-time-conditioned hierarchical dual-path memory-anchor retrieval mechanism. Guided by the effective age and semantic compatibility of historical information, it combines query-level candidate selection with point-level memory-anchor retrieval to provide historical evidence for sparse points at different forecast times. To better use memory anchors and existing features, a point-level residual adapter jointly gated by the task and forecast time separately controls residual corrections to semantics, occupancy confidence, and spatial positions. On Occ3D-nuScenes, MemAnchorWorld achieves an average mIoU of 13.55% and an average IoU of 22.84% across the 1-3 s forecasting horizons, attaining state-of-the-art performance on both metrics.Project page: https://memanchorworld.github.io/

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong results in arm-centric manipulation, yet humanoid whole-body control (WBC) requires dynamic balance and tightly coupled full-body coordination. To enable execution-aware differentiable training, we replace the non-differentiable simulator with a learned, action-conditioned world model, allowing multi-step body-execution losses to backpropagate through the frozen whole-body controller and the flow-matching sampler directly into the VLA action head. On four HumanoidArena simulation tasks, DiffGR00T improves average task success by 12.5 percentage points over the supervised base VLA (59.2% to 71.7%), demonstrating that execution-aware gradients effectively align high-level motion generation with closed-loop whole-body dynamics.

papers.title: Economic World Model
papers.abstract: Can artificial intelligence reproduce the economic dynamics that emerge as households, firms and governments interact and adapt through markets and institutions? To answer this question, we define an economic world model (EWM) as an agent's internal representation of how an economic system works, enabling counterfactual simulation and decision-making under resource constraints. We then propose a general framework for studying EWMs that links three tasks: simulating agent behaviour, learning economic transitions and systematically evaluating the dynamics. As an initial implementation, we learn household policies from microeconomic data and calibrate a structural economic transition model using macroeconomic data, linking individual decisions to aggregate dynamics. Our micro-to-macro evaluation framework compares simulated individual actions and group distributions with observed microdata and assesses macroeconomic dynamics through forecasting and counterfactual experiments. Results show that simulated and observed household consumption distributions overlap by 94.9%, while EWM forecasts closely track real GDP and several other aggregate levels. In government-borrowing counterfactuals, the EWM reproduces the benchmark life-cycle model's short-run transmission from borrowing to consumption. For ex ante planning, the EWM enables an LLM agent to achieve 10.29% higher simulated GDP under the epidemic shock than direct LLM decisions. This initial EWM is only a starting point. We invite economists and AI researchers to build a stronger EWM together. Economists can contribute richer economic models and knowledge, while AI researchers can develop stronger data-driven methods for simulating agent behaviour and learning economic transitions. Together, we aim not only to reproduce real economic dynamics, but also to discover and test new mechanisms that support better decisions and benefit society.

papers.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning. Meanwhile, most policy improvement methods learn dynamics and values in separate models, increasing training overhead and limiting representation sharing between these complementary objectives. We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretraining stage. Our key insight is that visual prediction encourages control-relevant features, while value supervision promotes task-relevant representations; together, they shape a representation suited to policy learning. Built on an image-editing backbone, DexWAC predicts, for each action chunk, the visual latent and proprioception at its endpoint together with its reward and continuation, so the world model alone efficiently yields complete imagined transitions without generating intermediate video frames. After adapting the world model and critic on real rollouts, we improve the pretrained actor through either PPO on imagined rollouts or critic-guided best-of-$N$ selection. DexWAC surpasses the large-scale pretrained VLA and WAM baselines in simulation and achieves 75% average success on two real-world tasks, compared with 45% for $π_{0.5}$. Its world model is more accurate and faster than video-based baselines, and ablations confirm that learning dynamics and value together improves the policy.

papers.title: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination
papers.abstract: Complex cooperative tasks require coordinated multi-agent behavior. Offline generative policies learn expressive cooperative behaviors from trajectories but remain limited by fixed datasets. Online reinforcement learning can improve them through environment interaction. However, fine-tuning flow policies is difficult because action likelihoods are hard to compute. We propose TeamFlowRL, a two-stage framework that pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online. We formulate team policy optimization over the complete denoising trajectories of decentralized flow policies, avoiding intractable action likelihoods. The resulting objective weights each agent's trajectory ratio with a shared team advantage and clips each ratio separately, aligning local policy updates with the common team return. Across 51 paired configurations in seven simulation groups, TeamFlowRL improves every offline initialization, with a 47.3% average gain in normalized score. It also achieves 33.1% higher average success under exploration noise than Gaussian-policy fine-tuning across 6 bimanual tasks.

papers.title: BARE: Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion for Humanoid Robots
papers.abstract: Dynamic obstacle avoidance is essential for safely deploying humanoid robots in real-world environments, where rapidly approaching objects require immediate evasive responses. Recent advances in reflexive evasion have focused primarily on quadrupeds, which typically rely on large-scale whole-body maneuvers. In contrast, humanoids can exploit their rich body articulation to evade through small, localized body adjustments. By moving threatened body regions without repositioning the entire body, these responses may require less execution time and less surrounding free space. However, local adjustments can alter mass distribution or support conditions, making it challenging to achieve rapid evasion while maintaining whole-body stability. To this end, we propose BARE (Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion), a humanoid reflexive evasion framework guided by human motion priors that enables rapid local evasion while maintaining whole-body stability. A risk-guided motion adapter is designed to select reference motions from a retargeted human evasive motion library based on the threatened body region and to adjust their temporal phases based on collision urgency, allowing the robot to reach evasive postures before potential contact. Conditioned on the adapted reference and link-level collision risk, a reflexive evasion policy learns through reinforcement learning to coordinate local body adjustments with whole-body stabilization. We validate BARE in simulation and real-world experiments, demonstrating its ability to perform targeted local evasion while maintaining whole-body stability.

papers.title: Assessing Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.abstract: As the use of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes more widespread in cyber-physical systems, it becomes increasingly important to design RL agents that are able to adapt to changes in their environments in order to maintain safety and reliability. This paper addresses the question of whether different classes of RL algorithm are more robust against forgetting previously learned behaviours, a critical issue in continual learning, in non-stationary environments. We evaluate the robustness of representative examples of three important classes of RL algorithm in a non-stationary autonomous parking environment. These are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which is a model-free on-policy algorithm, Soft-Actor-Critic (SAC), which is a model-free off-policy algorithm, and Drama, which is a model-based algorithm. The agents must learn to successfully park in four different scenarios, which are presented successively, with parking spaces oriented at varying angles. We find off-policy algorithms appear to be more robust compared to on-policy algorithms due to their use of replay, while model-based algorithms do not appear to offer any direct advantage over model-free algorithms. These experiments also highlight the additional challenges of finding robust abstractions of the environment, and oversensitivity to hyperparameters.

papers.title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Driving world models anticipate action consequences through representations of how the world evolves. For autonomous driving, these representations must capture both the surrounding scene and the ego vehicle's motion under a candidate plan. We propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that incorporates executable code as part of its world representation. Code represents ego dynamics by expressing how the vehicle state evolves under plan execution, while a learned visual model captures scene-dependent consequences. Executing the code produces a candidate-conditioned motion sequence, which is evaluated relative to the prior plan and recorded motion history. The resulting execution consequences and learned scene outcomes jointly represent the candidate's future, enabling the planner to assess both what a plan may lead to and how the vehicle transitions into that future. The selected plan becomes part of the next decision's execution context, linking successive choices within the model. CodeWAM achieves 93.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, 92.1 EPDMS on v2 navtest, and 50.6 EPDMS on NAVHARD. Further experiments demonstrate improved pairwise execution consistency and gains on Hydra-MDP and DrivoR without additional training, supporting executable code as a complementary representation for driving world models.

papers.title: CriticJEPA: World Models Are Better Critics Than Optimizers
papers.abstract: Visual world models enable goal-directed planning by predicting action outcomes. Gradient-based planners optimize actions to lower predicted goal cost, but continued optimization can exploit prediction errors after execution stops improving. Comparing plans requires informative relative scores; improving them also requires reliable update directions. Exact-state execution reveals that a frozen hierarchical world model ranks goal-conditioned proposals even when its rankings among outputs of prolonged gradient search are uninformative. Effective planning pairs goal-directed candidates with predictions that distinguish their outcomes. We introduce CriticJEPA, which learns goal-conditioned flow proposals from reward-free trajectories and uses frozen rollouts to select among them at every hierarchy level. Forward selection forms a complete planner; short anchored updates refine candidates before selection. Across visual navigation and manipulation, CriticJEPA increases success at a fraction of the planning compute, transferring shared settings across independently trained models, hierarchy depths, and unseen tasks while keeping every world-model weight fixed.

papers.title: DiCT: Teaching X-ray Vision-Language Models to Reason via Imagining CT
papers.abstract: Diagnosing with X-rays often requires reasoning about the 3D locations of abnormalities and their spatial relationships to surrounding anatomical structures, yet such reasoning remains challenging due to the loss of spatial information in 2D projections. To address this challenge, we propose Dreaming in CT (DiCT), a three-stage progressive CT-to-X-ray reasoning transfer framework that leverages a CT vision-language model (VLM) to guide an X-ray VLM. Through this CT-guided transfer, the student acquires CT-informed 3D reasoning capabilities, enabling it to reason directly from 2D X-rays without explicit CT reconstruction at inference time. The framework begins with instruct the dreamer, which equips the X-ray student with initial CT-oriented reasoning capabilities and establishes a structured interface that distinguishes X-ray observations from CT imagination. Building on this structure, visualize the dream introduces CT-guided on-policy distillation (OPD), where the CT teacher selectively guides the X-ray student's reasoning trajectories to transfer 3D anatomical knowledge. Finally, manifest the dream adapts the acquired reasoning capabilities from digitally reconstructed radiographs (DRRs) to real clinical X-rays. Experiments across two VLM backbones on 3D-RAD and ReXVQA demonstrate DiCT's effectiveness across radiological reasoning tasks, achieving a 1.66 percentage point improvement over a CT reconstruction-based baseline on 3D-RAD Abnormality Identification with 12.77$\times$ lower inference computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/HongYep/DiCT.

papers.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
papers.abstract: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout prediction versus performing rollout prediction before downsampling. We observe that fine-scale dynamical details are often encoded in this gap. By commuting these two operations, the fine-scale details removed during downsampling can be captured. Furthermore, we employ a memory module to store these fine-scale features along the trajectory and retrieve them during rollout, generating spatially adaptive corrections that enhance long-horizon fidelity. Empirical results across five systems demonstrate that CoMNO improves prediction accuracy and long-horizon rollout stability.

papers.title: Disentangling Visual Dynamics for World Model Planning
papers.abstract: Visual world models enable planning through predictive latent states. However, entangled agent and exogenous dynamics can obscure task progress. Disentangling visual dynamics for planning requires addressing two challenges: 1) suppressing cross-factor interference while retaining useful information; and 2) linking factors to task-relevant signals, since stability alone does not ensure meaningful planning distances. Therefore, we introduce FactorWorld, a disentangled visual dynamics framework for world model planning. To separate agent and exogenous dynamics, we propose a Counterfactual Consensus Residual Factorizer (CCRF) guided by bidirectional counterfactual pairs. CCRF separates shared context from dynamic residuals, combining average and worst-partner constraints to suppress interference with state and motion supervision to retain useful information. To translate these factors into planning decisions, we introduce semantic routing to refine full-representation task predictions for state estimation, trajectory scoring, and task-adapted planning. Experiments on MiniGrid, MetaDrive, and CARLA show improved bidirectional factor stability across two backbones. On MiniGrid, factor routing raises mean SR from 78.80% to 82.40%. Across four continuous control tasks, including Push-T, FactorWorld achieves mean success rates ranging from 91.67% to 100% across tasks. These results demonstrate that combining decoupled visual dynamics with explicit tasks can significantly improve the planning capabilities of world models.

papers.title: Relation Before Action: Explicit Relation Modeling for Latent Action Pretraining
papers.abstract: Learning latent actions from unlabeled video sequences offers a promising way to acquire reusable action representations without relying on embodiment-specific control annotations. However, existing latent-action pretraining approaches commonly couple the modeling of visual transitions with action inference, directly mapping paired observations or derived transition cues into latent action codes. This formulation leaves two distinct tasks entangled: characterizing the relational structure of an observed transition and abstracting it into a compact action representation. We propose RELACT, a relation-first framework that explicitly separates transition relation modeling from predictive action abstraction. RELACT first constructs a structured relation representation $R$ that captures how visual elements and their interactions evolve across observations. It then infers a compact, state-conditioned stochastic latent action $U$, whose predictive effects are learned through action-conditioned latent dynamics. The resulting action representation can be grounded in native control spaces for model-based planning or used to supervise downstream embodied policies. Extensive experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain image-goal navigation, goal-conditioned manipulation, and downstream policy adaptation demonstrate improved predictive action representations and consistent gains in planning and control, supporting the effectiveness and generality of relation-first latent action pretraining.

papers.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.

papers.title: SurgGenesis: A Generative Surgical World Model for Future-Aware Surgical Understanding
papers.abstract: Surgical scene understanding is constrained by data scarcity and long-tail class imbalance, as annotating surgical videos demands scarce clinical expertise while rare procedural events remain underrepresented. We tackle this through data generation and propose SurgGenesis, a generative surgical world model that learns future surgical state transitions in a latent space from visual observations and textual procedural descriptions, serving as a scalable surgical data engine. To adapt a large-scale video diffusion model to the data-scarce surgical domain without catastrophic forgetting, we introduce a three-stage progressive LoRA strategy that incrementally injects endoscopic visual priors, procedural semantics, and spatial motion cues. Rather than judging generation by visual fidelity alone, we validate SurgGenesis along two axes that separate a world model from a generic generator: (i) future-awareness, by comparing predicted futures against the real future through a GT-latent prediction gap and temporal-horizon analysis, and (ii) action-faithful usefulness, by checking that generated clips contain the commanded surgical triplet and that using them to rebalance long-tail events and drive downstream understanding (segmentation, triplet recognition, 3D reconstruction) yields action-specific gains. Conditioned futures therefore complement conventional long-tail sampling. Code: https://zh-qr.github.io/SurgGenesis

papers.title: Sounding the Black Box: Online Training of Embedded Neural Networks in Forward-Only Physical Simulators
papers.abstract: Hybrid physics-neural simulators embed neural networks in partial differential equation (PDE) solvers to model unresolved subgrid dynamics while preserving resolved physics and conservation laws. Because closure outputs feed back across time steps, single-step offline regression does not directly minimize multi-step rollout error, motivating online trajectory optimization. Solver backpropagation through time (BPTT) is the standard online solution when solver derivatives are available, yet many operational Fortran and C/C++ simulators expose only non-differentiable, forward-only interfaces. We introduce FORGE (Forward-Only Response and Gauss-Newton Estimation), an online framework that trains embedded networks from forward runs alone by decoupling exact network derivatives from black-box simulator dynamics. Stage I warms up the rollout via a low-dimensional Gauss-Newton step along output-orthonormal weight directions, canceling multi-layer feature drift via a final-layer correction. Stage II perturbs spatial output fields to fit a gain-bounded causal linear response operator across rollout steps, solves for regularized target outputs, and updates all weights via network backpropagation. Across five 2D and 3D benchmarks spanning phase separation, reaction-diffusion, fluid and MHD turbulence, and ocean circulation, FORGE outperforms gradient-free, reinforcement-learning, and emulator-based baselines, cutting coarse-solver test mean squared error (MSE) by 50%-96% in 2D and 70% in 3D, outperforming the strongest forward-only baseline by 16%-69%, and recovering 88%-98% of Solver BPTT's gains. Code is available at https://github.com/ChiyodaMomo01/FORGE.

papers.title: Learning When a Robot Should Ask For Help: Adaptive Intervention Requests in Human-Robot Teaming
papers.abstract: Robots operating in complex environments occasionally encounter situations where autonomous navigation fails. Requesting and receiving a timely intervention from their human supervisor can be critical for failure prevention or recovery. However, requesting help too frequently or at inappropriate times can increase operator workload and reduce team efficiency, while delayed requests may lead to prolonged downtime or unrecoverable failures. In addition to alert timing, the human, robot and task context also influences the intervention outcomes. This paper proposes an algorithm for learning to generate adaptive human intervention requests during human-robot teaming. A help-seeking policy is trained via offline reinforcement learning based on past intervention helpfulness and autonomous progress. This learned alert policy enables a robot to selectively request human help when the intervention outcome is likely to be beneficial. We evaluate the proposed policy in different task environments and user expertise levels in simulation, followed by evaluation in a physical user study. Our findings demonstrate that the learned policy improves exploration efficiency, reduces unnecessary alerts, and enhances novice user support without compromising expert performance in real-time human-robot teaming missions.

papers.title: ReJEPA: Bounded Predictive Regulation for Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models learn representations by predicting future states in an abstract embedding space rather than reconstructing raw pixels. When training across multi-frame sequences, however, not all frames and spatial regions are equally informative or predictable. We argue that forcing a world model to minimize every prediction error may be unnecessary and harmful. Under standard $L_2$ loss, unbounded gradients force the encoder and predictor to overfit noisy or transient frames at the expense of core physical structure, while amplifying gradient conflict with representation regularizers. Conversely, $L_1$ loss bounds large gradients, but its constant gradient magnitude near zero disrupts the local smoothness required for planning. We resolve this tension with \textbf{ReJEPA}, a bounded predictive regulation principle that combines bounded gradients for large errors with smooth quadratic behavior near zero, instantiated simply via the element-wise $\log\cosh$ loss.   As a drop-in training replacement across Temporal Straightening, LeWorldModel, and V-JEPA~2.1, $\log\cosh$ consistently outperforms $L_2$, a curvature-matched quadratic control, $L_1$, and Smooth-$L_1$ baselines without altering architectures or inference procedures. Notably, the gains grow with environmental complexity, scaling from simple navigation to contact-rich manipulation and real-world autonomous driving on NAVSIM. Probing and geometric analyses confirm that relaxing the penalty on extreme errors yields representations that better capture physical states and align with the true planning cost landscape.

papers.title: Co-DRIS: Physics-Informed Predictive Belief and Variable-Impedance Learning for Reactive Catching under Coupled Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Reactive robotic manipulation is acutely sensitive to simultaneous sensing noise, measurement dropouts, joint execution errors, and contact parameter variations. While single-frame frameworks like Domain-Randomized Instance Set (DRIS) achieve strong robustness under isolated uncertainties (86.4%), they degrade severely when perception and actuation uncertainties co-occur (27.6% across 10 coupled stress scenarios) due to memoryless encoding and fixed high-stiffness PD control. We propose Co-DRIS + SuperMimic, a perception-action co-design framework coupling: (i) an inertial world-frame physics-informed world model combining exact ballistic kinematics with a zero-initialized contact residual to roll forward missing observations and accelerate training via zero-cost counterfactual dropout consistency; (ii) an action-conditioned dual-stream causal GRU belief encoder resolving the denoising-vs-lag deadlock; and (iii) phase-aware variable-impedance soft-catching that transitions the 7-DoF Franka Research 3 arm into an overdamped regime (zeta/zeta0 ~ 2.26x) at the torque layer. Under unbiased 3-seed tail evaluation on unseen throws (15,360 throws/scenario), our method achieves 89.6 +/- 0.4% on standard benchmarks (+10.5% on 4-sigma noise to 70.5%) and 66.6 +/- 0.5% across 10 coupled/dropout stress scenarios (+39.0% over DRIS; +30.4% on 50% dropout). We further validate impedance decoupling, causal contact triggering under +0.65 s flight-time shifts, and cross-task transfer to steel-plate ping-pong bouncing (87.5% to 100.0%) and FR3+Hand catching (+8.4% under 4x noise with 6-13% lower peak impact force).

papers.title: Gaze World Model
papers.abstract: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode. This relationship is subtle, however, since an event far across the frame may produce only a slight movement of the person's head or eyes. We therefore introduce the Gaze World Model (GWM), which co-trains latent scene prediction with person-conditioned gaze supervision on a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder; in our ablations, the latent prediction objective improves both shift detection and gaze localization. Given a video clip and the person's head box, GWM estimates gaze locations and detects gaze shifts in the observed clip, and forecasts future gaze and shifts from predicted scene features. To train and evaluate these tasks, we augment VideoAttentionTarget and ChildPlay with event-level gaze-shift annotations. GWM achieves state-of-the-art shift detection on these benchmarks, about 10 points higher in four-class AP than the strongest baseline, while remaining comparable to the strongest image-based models in gaze target estimation, and outperforms the compared baselines on future gaze localization and shift forecasting.

papers.title: VG-GP: Uncertainty-Gated Visuo-Geometric Memory for Negative-Transfer-Resistant Grasp Adaptation
papers.abstract: Pretrained antipodal grasping networks generalize well to canonical shapes but frequently fail zero-shot on novel objects with irregular mass distributions, thin rims, or unfamiliar handles. While episodic experience memory adapts a frozen base policy without retraining, naive retrieval suffers from visual appearance bias, negative transfer from overriding working base grasps, and degenerate closed-loop acquisition. We present VG-GP, a plug-and-play Visuo-Geometric Gaussian Process memory framework for closed-loop $SE(2)$ residual grasp transfer. First, we fuse color-invariant surface-normal DINOv2 features, canonical $SE(2)$ gripper-aligned 3D local heightmaps, and contact-geometry descriptors under a product kernel with Automatic Relevance Determination (ARD) lengthscales learned strictly on source objects. Second, we model the joint posterior over the base grasp and candidate $SE(2)$ alternatives, overriding the base policy only when the joint-covariance Lower Confidence Bound (LCB) clears a risk-sensitive threshold. Third, an online counterfactual curation gate using single-record necessity and sufficiency interventions quarantines source experiences causing negative transfer. Fourth, we close the acquisition loop via Bayesian Expected Improvement (EI) over equal-budget $SE(2)$ probes. Across 42 disjoint YCB objects in ManiSkill3 (20 source, 12 development, 10 held-out test), VG-GP wraps a pretrained GR-ConvNet base policy and raises physical lift rate across all 22 unseen objects from 38.6% (34/88) to 53.4% (47/88) with zero regressions (+13 rescues, 0 losses; object-clustered 95% CI [+6.8%, +22.7%], exact McNemar $p = 0.00024$). On the 10 held-out objects, EI active acquisition reaches 45.0% (18/40 vs. 32.5% base, 5/7 of oracle headroom), achieves 55.0% probe divergence over passive fallback, and monotonically reduces epistemic uncertainty.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Coupled surge-pitch motions drive unsteady vortex interactions and dynamic wake meandering behind floating offshore wind turbines, complicating three-dimensional wake reconstruction from limited measurements and transfer across turbine scales. Large-eddy simulations coupled with an actuator line model generate fixed and surge-pitch wakes at motion-based Strouhal numbers $St=fD/U_\infty$ of 0.2-0.6 (where $f$, $D$, and $U_\infty$ are the motion frequency, rotor diameter, and inflow velocity) for the National Renewable Energy Laboratory 5 MW ($D=126$ m) and International Energy Agency 22 MW ($D=284$ m) turbines. A physics-informed Fourier neural operator framework combines four-dimensional spectral convolutions with incompressible continuity and rotor-forced momentum-residual regularization to reconstruct three-dimensional unsteady wakes from two observation planes. Trained on the 5 MW fixed and $St=0.2$-$0.5$ cases, the framework recovers near-wake double-peak deficits, motion-driven wake expansion, and coherent vortices through $St=0.6$ (mean wake-center and half-width errors within 1.3% and 1.0% of $D$), while 10% planar sampling preserves near-dense accuracy (relative $L_2$ error 0.0689 versus 0.0684). Applying transfer learning from the 5 MW to the 22 MW turbine lowers the three-dimensional streamwise-velocity error at $St=0.6$ by 36% relative to zero-shot inference (0.1066 to 0.0682), halves scratch-training error with one fixed case (0.0835 versus 0.1693), and restores wake-center tracking and motion-locked harmonics ($St$-$3St$). Large-scale motion-induced dynamics transfer cleanly across turbine scales, whereas fine-scale vortex breakdown remains damped. The framework shows potential for three-dimensional wake reconstruction and downstream-inflow assessment in floating wind farms.

papers.title: Dreamcatcher: Remembering What Surprises a World Model in Video Streams
papers.abstract: As live video streams grow longer, repeatedly encoding and processing their full histories becomes increasingly costly. Answering questions as they arrive therefore calls for visual memory built in one pass before future questions are known. Existing methods mainly keep tokens that differ from earlier ones or match surrogate queries fixed in advance. Without modeling world dynamics, these criteria struggle to tell subtle surprising details from expected change. We introduce Dreamcatcher, a training-free framework and, to our knowledge, the first to use predictive signals from an independently pretrained, frozen video world model for online memory formation in streaming video question answering. Conditioned on recent history, the world model predicts incoming features using learned world priors. Its normalized prediction errors yield temporal and spatial surprisal signals that guide online segmentation and the retention of a frozen Video-LLM's native visual tokens, balancing surprising details with broad visual coverage under budgets that decay with segment age. At query time, an evidence gate admits a segment from a similarity-based shortlist only when the Video-LLM judges that it adds evidence for the question beyond the current view. We evaluate Dreamcatcher on three streaming and three offline long-video benchmarks. On OVO-Bench, Dreamcatcher achieves the highest overall accuracy among the compared training-free methods for each of four frozen Video-LLMs, reaching 78.9% with Qwen3.8-27B. With the three Qwen Video-LLMs, it also reduces average input tokens for answer generation by more than 80% relative to their base models at 1 fps.

papers.title: Defect-Related Fatigue Anisotropy in Laser Powder Bed Fusion Ti–6Al–4V: Role of Sub-β-Transus Annealing and Build Orientation
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) Ti–6Al–4V shows orientation-dependent fatigue behavior that tensile properties and bulk density do not fully explain. Vertical (VT) and horizontal (HZ) specimens were annealed at 850 °C for 2 h (furnace cooling) and characterized by optical and scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD) with Rietveld refinement, micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), Vickers hardness, tensile tests, and high-cycle fatigue tests (R = 0.1). The annealed material consisted of α + β (approximately 88–92 vol.% α and 8–12 vol.% β). Tensile properties of the two orientations were similar, with HZ specimens slightly stronger and of similar elongation. Despite a bulk density above 99.9%, micro-CT revealed isolated pores of roughly 60–270 μm. At 600 MPa, VT specimens failed after 6.79 × 104 and 7.36 × 104 cycles, whereas HZ specimens failed after 8.82 × 105 and 1.37 × 106 cycles. Fatigue data at other stress levels are limited, so the orientation effect is demonstrated only at 600 MPa, where two specimens per orientation were tested. The results indicate that defect size, morphology, and orientation relative to the load, rather than tensile properties or density, are the likely cause of the anisotropy. An orientation-sensitive descriptor, F = dmax cos2θ, is proposed as a hypothesis; specimen-resolved defect data exist for only three VT specimens, so it remains to be validated. No as-built control was tested, and conclusions apply to the annealed condition.

papers.title: Artificial Neural Network-Based Surrogate Modelling for Finite Element Analysis of Automotive Mechanical Components
papers.abstract: Repeated finite element analyses (FEA) can dominate the computational cost of parametric structural studies, even when each individual simulation is linear and comparatively simple. Aiming to deliver an artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate model for standard FEA, this work develops pointwise ANNs capable of predicting mechanical response fields in two distinct automotive structural components. Finite element simulations were used to generate datasets for a two-dimensional bar-based automotive frame with geometric variations and for a two-dimensional continuum side guard support bracket. Multilayer perceptrons received nodal coordinates, geometric parameters and loading descriptors and predicted displacement components and individual nodal stress components. For the frame test sets, the homothetic network achieved R2=0.9995 and 0.9991 for ux and uy, respectively, while the stochastic network achieved R2=0.9899 and 0.9875. On complete reserved frame geometries, the total-displacement NRMSE was 0.8291% for the homothetic case and 2.9107% for the stochastic case. For the bracket, the displacement networks achieved R2=0.9996 and 0.9992, while the σxx, σyy and τxy networks achieved R2=0.8888, 0.9812 and 0.9397, respectively. Predicted unit-force displacement and stress-component fields were also combined by linear superposition under a realistic loading condition, yielding NRMSE values of 0.3250% and 0.4554% for Ux and Uy and 1.6620%, 2.1011% and 1.8611% for σxx, σyy and τxy, respectively. A computational break-even analysis indicated that the initial dataset generation and training costs were recovered after approximately 1094–1296 analyses for the frame models and 454–508 analyses for the bracket networks. The results support pointwise multilayer perceptrons as accurate surrogates for repeated linear structural analyses within the represented parametric domain.

papers.title: Single/Double Degree-of-Freedom Switching Mechanism and Performance Verification of a Reconfigurable Quadruped Wheeled Robot
papers.abstract: In this paper, a quadrupedal wheeled robot with reconfigurable single- and double-degree-of-freedom (DOF) modes is proposed, which is accomplished by knee joint folding and the use of mechanical limiters, without requiring any additional locking components. The lower leg is folded against a mechanical stop and a holding torque is applied to restrict the leg to a single degree of freedom for flat ground wheeling, while the stop is released to allow the leg to move with two degrees of freedom in the hip and knee for legged obstacle traversal. Kinematic and finite element models are created, and MuJoCo simulations are performed using a unified robot description format (URDF) model, which uses reinforcement learning to generate walking gaits. The double-DOF mode increases the maximum foot span by 24% (to 0.411 m) and provides 41% more clearance in the vertical direction, and the workspace changes from a one-dimensional arc to a two-dimensional (2D) area. The chassis, joint output shafts and limiters are not stressed beyond their material yield strengths with rated payloads of 20 kg and safety factors of 2.7–4.0. The robot was able to complete the five 20 s trials without falling, making a journey of approximately 1.94 m with an average speed of 0.098 m/s, and peak joint torques that were within the 25 N·m limit. These results confirm the kinematic and simulation feasibility of the mechanism, while prototype validation of repeated switching, load holding, and actual obstacle traversal remains to be completed.

papers.title: Differentiable modeling for constitutive surface identification of time–temperature dependent viscoelastic behavior in asphalt mixtures
papers.abstract: Inferring the time–temperature-dependent viscoelastic behavior of asphalt mixtures from structural response observations is an intrinsically challenging inverse problem, often exhibiting ill-posed characteristics. Conventional approaches typically rely on predefined functional forms, which impose restrictive assumptions, introduce structural bias in the inferred material behavior, and often lead to challenging and sensitive parameter calibration. This study presents a differentiable modeling framework for physics-constrained identification of a continuous time–temperature-dependent modulus surface E(t,T). Within this framework, the unknown modulus surface is represented by a neural network and embedded within a finite element formulation. The forward model explicitly solves the discretized equilibrium equations under prescribed loading and boundary conditions, and gradients of the response-level loss are propagated through the solver to update the modulus representation. By avoiding fixed constitutive functional forms while retaining the mechanics constraints of the finite element model, the proposed formulation enables direct inference of a unified time–temperature-dependent modulus surface from structural observations. The framework is validated using controlled numerical experiments with known modulus surfaces, noisy response observations, and independent experimental creep data from the literature. Its performance is further benchmarked against a conventional Prony-series-based baseline and a PINN-based inverse modeling approach. The results demonstrate accurate reconstruction, stable convergence under noise, and consistent recovery of the time–temperature stiffness evolution within the considered loading protocol and observation window. Overall, the proposed framework provides a solver-coupled, physics-constrained pathway for inverse characterization of asphalt mixture behavior directly from structural responses.

papers.title: An extended fluid–structure interaction framework for aortic hemodynamics and cardiovascular risk assessment using physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with aortic pathologies posing significant risk due to their complex hemodynamic and biomechanical interactions. Accurate evaluation of intravascular pressure and wall mechanics is therefore essential for reliable risk assessment. In this study, we propose a hybrid fluid–structure interaction (FSI) and physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for efficient and physics-consistent prediction of aortic hemodynamics. High-fidelity two-way FSI simulations are first performed to capture the coupled interaction between pulsatile blood flow and arterial wall deformation. The resulting spatiotemporal velocity and pressure fields are subsequently combined with the governing flow equations and associated physical constraints within a hybrid FSI–PINN framework for physics-informed pressure reconstruction. Rather than relying on fluid-only CFD datasets that neglect arterial wall compliance and its bidirectional coupling with blood flow, the proposed framework is trained on fully coupled fluid–structure interaction (FSI) simulations, thereby embedding fluid–solid interaction physics directly into the learning process. The trained PINN accurately reconstructs three-dimensional pressure fields across the aortic domain, achieving a maximum relative error below 1% compared to the FSI reference solution, while maintaining robustness under sparse and noisy data conditions. In addition to high accuracy, the proposed framework significantly reduces relative computational expense, enabling rapid inference without the need for repeated FSI simulations. These results demonstrate the potential of the FSI–PINN approach as a computationally efficient and physiologically consistent surrogate model for cardiovascular hemodynamic analysis and risk assessment.

papers.title: Case Report: One-stage comprehensive reconstruction for intrapelvic cup migration with Paprosky IIIB acetabular bone loss and Vancouver B3 periprosthetic femoral fracture after total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Complex late mechanical failure after total hip arthroplasty (THA) may involve not only periprosthetic fracture (PPF), but also severe acetabular bone loss, component migration, and femoral stem loosening. When these mechanically interrelated failure modes coexist, fracture-centered treatment alone may be insufficient to restore the stability of the entire hip construct. A 77-year-old woman presented with acute functional deterioration 24 years after primary THA. Her preoperative visual analog scale (VAS) pain score was 8 and Harris Hip Score (HHS) was 20. Preoperative imaging demonstrated Paprosky type IIIB acetabular bone loss, intrapelvic cup migration, and femoral stem loosening, but no definite proximal femoral fracture line was identifiable. A greater trochanteric fracture was identified during surgical exposure before removal of the original stem. The femoral fracture was classified as Vancouver type B3 based on intraoperative confirmation of a grossly loose stem and substantial proximal femoral bone loss. No fall or other identifiable trauma preceded the acute deterioration. Preoperative testing showed an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 30 mm/h, C-reactive protein (CRP) of 7.77 mg/L, and white blood cell (WBC) count of 7.0 × 10^9/L; no joint aspiration was performed, and occult infection could not be definitively excluded. One-stage reconstruction used two Trabecular Metal augments, a 64-mm porous-metal revision shell, a distally fixed Wagner SL revision stem, and hook plate-cable fixation to address acetabular, femoral implant, and fracture instability. At 9 months, the implants remained stable without radiographic loosening, migration, or dislocation, with progressive fracture healing. The VAS score decreased to 3, the HHS improved to 91, and the patient regained independent ambulation. This case highlights the importance of extending treatment planning beyond fracture-centered management toward assessment of the entire arthroplasty construct when severe acetabular bone loss, component migration, femoral stem loosening, and PPF coexist. Identifying and simultaneously addressing each source of mechanical instability may provide a rational basis for individualized one-stage reconstruction in selected patients.

papers.title: Crystallinity-Driven Structure–Property Relationships in 3D-Printed Silk Fibroin/Poly(l - co -D, l -lactic acid) Scaffolds for Tissue Engineering
papers.abstract: Hybrid natural–synthetic polymer systems offer a strategy to combine the biological properties of natural polymers with the tunable physicochemical characteristics of synthetic polymers for tissue engineering applications. In this study, an extrusion-printable hybrid ink based on silk fibroin (SF) and poly(l-co-D,l-lactic acid) (PLDLA) was developed, and the effect of PLDLA content on the properties and printability of the resulting scaffolds was investigated. SF/PLDLA formulations were prepared with a fixed SF concentration of 15 wt % and PLDLA contents ranging from 0 to 15 wt %, and evaluated in terms of rheological and viscoelastic behavior, printability, molecular organization, crystallinity and cytocompatibility. Increasing PLDLA content progressively increased the viscosity and enhanced the viscoelastic character of the formulations, while preserving their structural recovery after shear. These changes supported extrusion processing and allowed the fabrication of well-defined structures, with the formulations containing 5 and 7 wt % PLDLA showing the most suitable printing behavior. FTIR analysis indicated the physical incorporation of PLDLA into the SF matrix and an increase in β-sheet content, while WAXD revealed a progressive increase in crystallinity with increasing PLDLA concentration. Thermal analyses further suggested interactions between the polymeric components. All formulations maintained cell viability above 70% after 72 h, with regular cell morphology and evidence of cell proliferation. Overall, PLDLA incorporation provided an effective means of modulating the rheological and structural characteristics of SF-based inks while maintaining cytocompatibility. These findings demonstrate the potential of SF/PLDLA natural–synthetic hybrid inks for the fabrication of extrusion-printed scaffolds with composition-dependent properties for tissue engineering applications.

papers.title: Aspects diagnostiques et thérapeutiques de la coxarthrose de l’adulte à l’Hôpital National Amirou Boubacar Diallo de Niamey
papers.abstract: Introduction :Coxarthrosis is a degenerative process of the cartilage of the hip joint. Aim: to describe the epidemiological, clinical, radiological, therapeutic and outcome features of hip osteoarthritis in adults at the Amirou Boubacar Diallo National Hospital (HNABD), Niamey.Materials and methods :retrospective descriptive study of the records of patients aged 18 years or older treated for hip osteoarthritis from 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2021; radiological assessment according to Kellgren and Lawrence and functional assessment with the Postel and Merle d’Aubigné (PMA) score.Results :a total of 58 patients were included. Male patients accounted for 55.17%. The mean age was 34.67 years. The mean duration of symptoms was 24.77 months. Pain was present in all patients. The PMA score was poor in 30 patients. Walking distance was limited in 52 patients. According to the Kellgren and Lawrence classification, 42 patients were at stage IV. Secondary osteoarthritis accounted for 62.07% of cases, mainly due to sickle cell-related aseptic osteonecrosis of the femoral head (27/36 secondary forms, i.e. 46.55% of all patients). Arthroplasty was performed in 32 patients. Seven complications (12.07%) were recorded during hospital follow-up; at last follow-up, 3 cotyloiditis after hemiarthroplasty and 2 cup loosenings after total hip arthroplasty were found. At the last follow-up, the PMA score was very good in 13 of the 20 patients reviewed.Conclusion :hip osteoarthritis in adults at HNABD affects young patients, is mostly secondary, mainly to sickle cell osteonecrosis, and is diagnosed at an advanced stage; assessment of treatment outcomes requires structured prospective follow-up.
