papers.title: Periprosthetic femoral fracture risk varies across cemented femoral stem designs: a nationwide Swiss joint registry study
papers.abstract: Purpose Cemented fixation is associated with lower periprosthetic femoral fracture (PPFx) risk than uncemented fixation; however, risk variations between cemented stem fixation philosophies remain unclear. Using data from the Swiss National Joint Registry (SIRIS), this nationwide study compared PPFx risk among different cemented femoral stem designs used in primary hip arthroplasty. Methods A total of 290,639 primary arthroplasties performed between 2012 and 2025 were identified in SIRIS. Cemented stems were classified into Type 1 traditional (Type 1t) taper-slip with a distal centralizer, Type 1 fit-and-fill (Type 1ff), or Type 2 composite beam designs. Multivariable Cox regression models assessed associations between stem design and PPFx risk, stratified by indication (osteoarthritis versus fracture) and adjusted for age and sex. Results Among 290,639 primary arthroplasties, 2149 (0.74%) were revised for PPFx. Cemented fixation was associated with a lower risk than uncemented fixation in both osteoarthritis (hazard ratio (HR) 0.30–0.70) and fracture patients (HR 0.26–0.74). In THA for osteoarthritis, Type 2 composite beams stems showed the lowest fracture risk and remained superior to Type 1ff stems after multivariable adjustment (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.41–0.97). Type 1t stems were associated with a lower risk in primary analysis but not after additional adjustment. In fracture patients, no significant differences were observed between cemented stem designs. Male sex (HR 1.62–1.67) and age ≥ 80 years (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.20–2.32) were associated with a higher risk. Type 2 performed best in osteoarthritis, while no differences were observed in fracture patients. Conclusion Cemented fixation was associated with a lower PPFx risk, but not uniformly across designs. In osteoarthritis, Type 2 composite-beam stems showed the most robust risk reduction compared with Type 1ff fit-and-fill stems, despite Type 1ff being the most used design in Switzerland. In fracture patients, no cemented design was superior.

papers.title: Surgical approach impacts patient-reported symptoms following arthroplasty for femoral neck fractures
papers.abstract: Aims: We aimed to compare outcomes between patients with displaced femoral neck fractures (FNFs) managed with total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty (HA) via an anterolateral/lateral compared with posterior approach. Methods: We used data from the Hip fracture Evaluation with Alternatives of Total hip arthroplasty versus Hemiarthroplasty (HEALTH) trial, which randomized 1,441 patients aged 50 years and older with displaced femoral neck fractures to receive THA or HA. We calculated each patient's propensity to undergo arthroplasty via posterior approach, and matched each patient to one control (anterolateral/lateral approach) based on age (SD 5 years), BMI (SD 3 points), and propensity score (using a caliper of 0.2 SDs). We used chi-squared and Fisher's exact tests to compare dichotomous outcomes between matched groups, and repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to examine differences in patient-reported outcomes at baseline and one year postoperatively. We used logistic regression to identify independent predictors of reoperation for instability in the posterior group. Results: A total of 1,306 patients met the inclusion criteria; 876 (67.1%) received arthroplasty via an anterolateral/lateral approach, and 430 (32.9%) through posterior approach. Following propensity score matching, we retained 790 patients, 395 in each group, with no differences in patient, fracture, or implant characteristics. The rate of treatment for dislocation was higher in the posterior approach group. Repeated measures ANOVA revealed significantly better Western Ontario and McMaster Universities osteoarthritis index (WOMAC) pain, stiffness, function, and total scores in the posterior group. We identified THA (vs HA, odds ratio (OR) 2.05, 95% CI 1.05 to 4.01) and being a primary wheelchair ambulator or bedridden (OR 3.27, 95% CI 1.29 to 8.29) as independent predictors of reoperation for instability in the posterior group. Conclusion: Our analyses suggest that patients with displaced FNFs who undergo arthroplasty via the posterior approach may report better symptoms and functional outcomes at one year compared with an anterolateral/lateral approach, despite increased risk of reoperation for instability. Further prospective studies comparing anterolateral/lateral and posterior approaches for arthroplasty following femoral neck fracture would be beneficial.

papers.title: Crack Propagation and Suppression in Fused Silica During CO 2 Laser Polishing: A Numerical Investigation
papers.abstract: As a critical optical component, achieving crack‐free surfaces on fused silica through CO 2 laser polishing remains challenging due to residual stresses induced by steep thermal gradients. This study aims to elucidate the mechanisms of crack initiation and propagation during this process. A three‐dimensional multiphysics model coupling temperature and stress fields was developed and validated experimentally (< 5% error). Crack propagation was simulated using the extended finite element method (XFEM), analyzing the effects of crack size, location, and interaction. The maximum residual von Mises stress after laser polishing was 26.35 MPa. Combined with the subsequent XFEM fracture analysis, the results suggest that crack development cannot be attributed to the overall residual stress level alone and that pre‐existing defects play an important role in crack initiation and propagation. Terminal‐edge cracks exhibited significantly greater propagation (e.g., 1380 μm for a 100‐μm crack) than central cracks due to heat accumulation. Collinear cracks showed a 51% reduction in propagation length (340 μm vs. 700 μm) due to stress shielding. Implementing a 900°C isothermal preheating strategy effectively reduced the thermal gradient, suppressing crack propagation length by 70% (from 400 to 120 μm).

papers.title: Primary reconstruction of posterior wall acetabular fractures using a 3D printed titanium alloy prosthesis in a pre-clinical canine model
papers.abstract: Posterior wall acetabular fractures (PWF) are the most common type of acetabular fractures, yet their outcomes are often unsatisfactory, especially with comminution and marginal impaction. This experimental animal study assessed the feasibility and effectiveness of primary posterior wall reconstruction using a 3D printed titanium alloy prosthesis. Six healthy male Beagle dogs, aged one year, were selected. Six dogs served as their own control. The left acetabular posterior wall underwent primary reconstruction with the 3D printed prosthesis (experimental group), while the right side received primary fixation with a reconstruction plate (control group). Radiographic evaluation, including pelvic X-ray and CT scans, were performed at six and 12 weeks postoperatively. At 12 weeks, hip joint specimens were harvested for gross necropsy and histological examination, focusing on bone formation and microscopic wear of the femoral heads. Micro-CT analysis was used to assess bone ingrowth in the prostheses. Postoperative radiographic imaging at six and 12 weeks indicated that acetabular congruence with the femoral head was maintained in both groups. Gross necropsy showed continuous and intact articular surface in both groups. There were no significant differences in macroscopic or microscopic wear of the femoral head between the two groups ( p > 0.05). New bone occupied 31.2% of the prosthesis-bone interface in the experimental group and 70.1% of the fracture site in the control group. Micro-CT analysis in the experimental group revealed substantial bone trabecular ingrowth and osseointegration at the prosthesis-bone interface, with a bone volume tissue volume ratio (BV/TV) of 31.8%. Primary posterior wall reconstruction using a 3D printed titanium alloy prosthesis was feasible and effective in the animal experiment as it restored a congruent and stable articular segment; objective functional outcomes remain to be evaluated in future studies. papers.title: A physics-informed neural network (PINN) for 2D crack analysis
papers.abstract: This paper presents an application of physics-informed neural networks PINNs to solve two-dimensional (2D) fracture mechanics problems within the framework of linear elasticity. Unlike traditional mesh-based numerical methods such as the finite element method (FEM), PINNs incorporate the governing partial differential equations, specifically the Navier-Cauchy equilibrium equations, directly into the neural network loss function. This approach eliminates the need for complex mesh generation and refinement around the crack tip. The methodology incorporates constitutive relations, displacement boundary conditions, and traction-free crack surface conditions into a multi-objective optimization problem. To address the inherent stress singularities and displacement discontinuities at the crack tip, specialized domain transformations or enrichment strategies are integrated into the deep learning architecture. Numerical simulations are conducted for standard mode I crack benchmarks. The results demonstrate that the proposed PINNs framework can accurately predict displacement fields and stress distributions with high fidelity compared to analytical solutions. Furthermore, the mesh-free nature of PINNs offers significant advantages for handling irregular geometries and has potential for inverse fracture analysis in structural integrity assessments. The study concludes that PINNs offer a robust and efficient alternative for modeling fracture behavior in solid mechanics without the computational overhead of traditional remeshing techniques.

papers.title: In Vitro Cytocompatibility and In Vivo Local Tissue Response of Titanium Implants Coated with 3D-Printed Hydroxyapatite–Collagen (HAp-COL) for Orbital Fractures: A Preliminary Study
papers.abstract: Orbital wall reconstruction with titanium meshes provides mechanical support, but the bio-inert metal surface limits osseointegration and may favor soft-tissue entrapment. This study evaluated a nanostructured hydroxyapatite–collagen (HAp-COL) hybrid derived from Rapana thomasiana (syn. Rapana venosa) shells as a 3D-printed coating for titanium orbital implants. The hybrid powder (HAp:COL mass ratio of 4:1) was obtained via high-pressure hydrothermal synthesis and spray drying and characterized using FAAS, ICP-OES, XRD, SEM–EDS, DLS, and DSC–TG. A solvent-free paste with polyvinyl alcohol and aqueous polyurethane binders was robocast at room temperature onto titanium meshes. Cytocompatibility was assessed using MTT assays on normal human osteoblasts, murine Swiss 3T3 fibroblasts, and adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). Local tolerance was evaluated in a rabbit orbital bone defect model over 2 months. The powder was mainly crystalline hydroxyapatite with minor whitlockite (Ca:P = 1.68; Z-average hydrodynamic diameter: 75.81 nm). Cell viability exceeded the 70% threshold under all conditions except undiluted extracts on MSCs at 24 h (66.63%), which recovered to 75.47% at 48 h. In a single experiment, robocast HAp-COL coatings showed numerically higher osteoblast viability values (80.61–96.47%) than sprayed HAp coatings (70.62–93.63%). Descriptive histology and CD31/CD34 immunohistochemistry showed fibrovascular colonization and neovascularization without necrosis. These preliminary results indicate cytocompatibility and short-term local tissue tolerance; osteogenic activity, osseointegration, and the mechanical reliability of the coating remain to be demonstrated in controlled studies.

papers.title: Beyond compliance: performance on a simulation-led, gated pre-laboratory health and safety worksheet in biomedical education
papers.abstract: Background Traditional higher education approaches to laboratory health and safety often rely on passive instruction, failing to build real-world competency. Consequently, undergraduate students frequently view safety compliance as a bureaucratic hurdle, resulting in poor engagement. Methods We implemented an active learning pre-laboratory experience using a simulated, ICT-assessed “Smart Worksheet” developed with LearnSci for a cohort of Year 1 biomedical science undergraduates (n = 46). Access to physical laboratory sessions was gated by completion of the online activity. Students were required to extract critical regulatory data from non-standardised, multi-supplier Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) to complete digital Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH) forms and execute a de novo Risk Assessment. Results Worksheet performance differed significantly across the four sections (Friedman, P < 0.001). Mean scores were higher in Sect. 3 than in Sect. 1 (76.1% vs. 58.3%; P = 0.000000004), consistent with familiarisation, although this cannot be attributed to repetition alone. papers.title: Physics-informed Neural Networks for Fast Multilayer Spectral Inversion of H α 6562.8 Å and Ca II 8542.1 Å Spectra
papers.abstract: Strong chromospheric absorption lines diagnose solar plasma dynamics and thermal structure, but conventional multilayer spectral inversion (MLSI) requires costly pixel-by-pixel nonlinear fitting. We introduce a physics-informed neural network (MLSI-PINN) that accelerates MLSI while retaining its analytic radiative-transfer formulation. The network predicts parameters from observed profiles and reconstructs spectra through a differentiable forward model. Training first minimizes the spectral reconstruction loss, then adds parameter supervision from conventional MLSI inversions of one reference raster, reducing the need for large precomputed training sets. Applied to quiet-Sun and active-region H α 6562.8 Å and Ca II 8542.1 Å observations from the Fast Imaging Solar Spectrograph (FISS) at the Goode Solar Telescope (GST), MLSI-PINN reproduces the main spatial structures of conventional MLSI parameter maps, with an arithmetic mean of 0.933 across the reported pixel-wise Pearson correlation coefficients. Reconstructed spectra remain close to observations and MLSI reconstructions. After training, the complete workflow takes 5–15 s per raster, compared with 3–5 minutes for conventional MLSI, giving a 12–60-fold speedup. For prepared inputs, parameter retrieval, including the photospheric-velocity estimate, takes approximately 0.6 s, giving a 300–500-fold speedup excluding input loading and output storage. These results support efficient MLSI analysis of large spectroscopic datasets. The code and supporting materials are available on GitHub (https://github.com/ZY-NJ/MLSI-PINN).

papers.title: Automatically calibrated on-chip continuously tunable dispersion compensator for high-speed quantum key distribution system in networks
papers.abstract: High-speed quantum key distribution (QKD) systems are intrinsically sensitive to chromatic dispersion, necessitating precise compensation. Furthermore, practical quantum networks demand dynamically tunable solutions to adapt to diverse and fluctuating channel conditions. To address these critical challenges, we demonstrate an automatically calibrated and continuously tunable on-chip dispersion compensator utilizing sixth-order cascaded thin-film lithium niobate microrings. To overcome the complex multistage thermal crosstalk inherent in such cascaded structures, we develop a hybrid calibration algorithm that combines Bayesian optimization for a global search across varying target link lengths with simulated annealing for local fine-tuning. In a 1.25 GHz proof-of-principle QKD system, our device robustly restores interference visibility to over 95% across fiber links ranging from 75 to 125 km, successfully rescuing severely degraded visibility from as low as approximately 71%. This work provides a robust and scalable solution for dynamic dispersion management, facilitating the practical implementation of high-performance quantum networks.

papers.title: The role of Bayesian statistics in the age of AI
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models and deep neural networks, is transforming prediction, representation learning, and scientific workflows. This essay argues that AI does not diminish the importance of Bayesian statistics; it sharpens the need for uncertainty quantification, principled information sharing, incorporation of prior knowledge, interpretability, and decision making under uncertainty. Deep learning is often invaluable for extracting structure from complex raw data, but scientific applications require reliable uncertainty assessments and transparent inferential reasoning. The essay considers Bayesian perspectives on foundation models and AI‐assisted research, teaching, and collaboration, and argues that Bayesian statisticians should engage actively with AI while maintaining critical oversight. As AI is deployed in increasingly consequential scientific settings, Bayesian reasoning remains central to making its outputs trustworthy and useful.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of the Active and Meaningful Learning Model Integrated with Monomath Gamification in Enhancing Students’ Mathematical Conceptual Understanding
papers.abstract: This study aims to design and examine the effectiveness of the Active & Meaningful Learning (AML) model integrated with Monomath gamification media in enhancing students’ mathematical conceptual understanding in senior/vocational high school. The research was conducted in Grade XI at SMA Negeri 1 Pabelan and SMK Diponegoro Salatiga using research and development with the ADDIE Model. This study produced the syntax of the AML Model integrated with Monomath Gamification. The AML model combines principles of active learning and meaningful learning through five phases: activation, organizing, exploration, meaningful integration, and evaluation. Monomath, an adaptation of the Monopoly board game with an archipelago theme, was designed to be flexible across mathematical topics and to promote cognitive, affective, and psychomotor engagement. In terms of validity, evaluations from two expert validators confirmed that the model is in the “very valid” category, with material validity scores ranging from 95,71% to 97,14% and media validity scores of 86.20% and 89.65%. In the preliminary field testing, the significance value of the Independent Samples Mann-Whitney test was 0.000 < 0.05, and in the main field testing, the significance value of the Related Samples Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test was 0.000 < 0.05. This means that the AML Model integrated Monomath Gamification had a significant effect on the mathematical conceptual understanding of Grade XI students SMA Negeri 1 Pabelan and SMK Diponegoro Salatiga. The findings indicate that the AML model integrated with Monomath effectively enhances students’ conceptual understanding and increases learning engagement, creating an interactive, meaningful, and enjoyable mathematics learning environment. Keywords: active and meaningful learning (AML), monomath gamification, mathematical conceptual understanding; game-based learning; mathematics education.

papers.title: Comparing acquisition function optimization methods in combinatorial Bayesian optimization for chemical materials discovery
papers.abstract: The optimization of expensive-to-evaluate black-box functions over combinatorial structures is a common task in machine learning, materials science, and physics. Bayesian optimization for combinatorial optimization problems has recently been proposed to address such black-box optimization problems. In these methods, the surrogate function is often represented as a second-order model and formulated as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem. In Bayesian optimization, the construction and optimization of the acquisition function, which determines the next evaluation point of the black-box function, are crucial for balancing “exploration” and “exploitation.” Quantum annealing, which leverages quantum fluctuations to search for solutions, has attracted significant attention as a metaheuristic for QUBO problems. Recently, the properties of solutions obtained by quantum annealing have also drawn substantial interest, and there is active research on ways to utilize these solutions. In this paper, we tackle the optimization of a black-box function with combinatorial structure, motivated by the search for real chemical materials. We present results comparing quantum annealing with simulated annealing, which leverages thermal fluctuations. We investigate how the optimization method and its accuracy in optimizing the acquisition function affect Bayesian optimization. As a result, in our problem setting, when we used quantum annealing, the outcomes did not depend strongly on the annealing time, and Bayesian optimization performed well, balancing “exploration” and “exploitation.” This allowed us to discover numerous input points whose material property values were at or above the desired threshold. We also confirmed that simulated annealing exhibited behavior similar to quantum annealing under a specific annealing schedule.

papers.title: Methods of ICS/OT communication model recovery from cyber-physical systems observations
papers.abstract: The defense of cyber-physical systems in the ICS/OT segment of critical infrastructure faces unique challenges, stemming from the prioritization of availability, order-of-magnitude longer maintenance cycles than in IT, and significant limitations on active defense methods. Specific industrial control protocols require different intrusion detection and prevention network tools; the most effective ones are capable of deep protocol analysis, baseline recovery via learning, and anomaly detection through deviations from said baseline. The last two points lead to the need for a communication model recovery, including normal parameter ranges, typical operations, etc. In the absence of developer documentation, large codebases of proprietary software and firmware without source code, protocol reverse engineering, and communication modeling may be difficult tasks. In this work, we propose novel methods for recovering a communication model that fuse heterogeneous sources, such as passive network monitoring data, video streams from operating equipment, and HMI screencasts. Proposed methods are implemented in an autonomous agentic system capable of working in an air-gapped network and producing a communication model description with Python 3.10+ client source code for remote industrial equipment control. Model capabilities have been validated on the Igor Sikorsky KPI ICS\&AI Security Laboratory testbed using real hardware. During the validation stage, modern open-weight LLMs were benchmarked, and a data-driven approach to provider architecture choice was implemented. We improve the state of the art in safe active learning under real-time and safety constraints of cyber-physical systems in critical infrastructure.

papers.title: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning and Model Predictive Control for Cooperative Car-Following in Autonomous Vehicle Platoons Under Onboard Sensing and V2V Communication
papers.abstract: Autonomous platoons rely on onboard sensors and vehicle-to-vehicle telemetry to maintain safe gaps, yet static model predictive control (MPC) cannot adapt spacing across transients, whereas unconstrained deep reinforcement learning (DRL) lacks safety guarantees. This paper develops a hierarchical DRL–MPC framework under a predecessor–leader–follower topology. A parameter-shared soft actor-critic agent adapts tracking-to-control weight ratio, active horizon, and desired time headway online, projecting actions onto a three-dimensional string-stable manifold capping the semi-analytical passband peak gain at 0.985, while a sparse quadratic program enforces kinematic limits with comfort slack and emergency fallback. Across the nominal eight-scenario suite and five seeds, it achieves 100% solver feasibility, zero safety violations, and passband compliance across all 15,720 operating points, while surviving 15 tight-gap stress runs with zero collisions. It reduces the mean gap by 10.9% and 24.8% compared with fixed MPC (1.20 s) and ACC/CACC (1.50 s), respectively, driven by the lower mean headway. Against passband-compliant projected static MPC (1.075 s) and headway-matched fixed MPC (1.00 s), online adaptation raises worst-case minimum time-to-collision from 5.74 s and 5.30 s to 6.88 s, with an RMSE of 1.90 m, a jerk of 1.19 m/s3, a string ratio of 1.113 (detrended: 1.024; cruise S6: 1.298), and a runtime of 27.54 ms vs. 14.64 ms (1.00 s MPC).

papers.title: PENINGKATAN LITERASI EKONOMI SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR MELALUI PROJECT-BASED LEARNING BERBANTUAN POT GERABAH
papers.abstract: The economic literacy of fifth-grade students is currently below expectations, which was identified through preliminary observation data. This is primarily due to theoretical learning processes that lack contextual relevance. To address this issue, this study aims to analyze the improvement of elementary school students' economic literacy through the implementation of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model assisted by local pottery commodities. This quantitative study utilized a quasi-experimental non-equivalent pre-test post-test control group design involving an experimental class and a control class selected via cluster random sampling. Data were collected using a multiple-choice objective test instrument, consisting of 20 valid items confirmed through content validity testing. A population equivalence test (ANOVA) was conducted using pre-test data to ensure group comparability. Data analysis applied descriptive and inferential statistics, specifically a pooled variance t-test calculated with population variance (VAR.P). The research results demonstrated a significant enhancement, where the experimental group achieved a post-test average that met the Criterion-Referenced Assessment (PAP) standards. Statistical analysis revealed that the t-count exceeded the t-table value, meaning the null hypothesis was rejected. These findings confirm that integrating local commodities into project-based learning significantly optimizes students' comprehension of economic concepts. The implication of this study is that educators should adopt contextualized, active learning strategies to effectively foster economic literacy skills.

papers.title: The Application of 3D-printing Technology in Engineering Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing, commonly known as 3D printing, has become an important manufacturing approach for producing complex geometries, customised components, prototypes, and low-volume parts directly from digital models. This paper reviews the basic principles, major process categories, engineering applications, and current limitations of 3D printing in modern manufacturing. Four representative technologies—Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM), Stereolithography (SLA), Selective Laser Sintering (SLS), and Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF, often referred to as SLM)—are compared in terms of material systems, forming mechanisms, accuracy, surface quality, support requirements, mechanical performance, post-processing, cost, and suitable applications. Their use in automotive engineering, aerospace manufacturing, mechanical equipment production, tooling, prototyping, and small-batch functional components is further discussed. The analysis shows that additive manufacturing provides clear advantages where geometric complexity, rapid iteration, customisation, and tooling reduction are important. However, equipment and material costs, limited printable material ranges, process-induced defects, anisotropic properties, quality-control challenges, and extensive post-processing continue to restrict broader industrial adoption. Therefore, additive manufacturing is more appropriately regarded as a complementary technology to conventional machining, casting, and mould-based manufacturing rather than a universal replacement.

papers.title: Consumer-Informed Formulation and Exploratory Bayesian Optimization of a Cassava-Based Biscuit Containing Momordica charantia Seed Oil and Press Cake
papers.abstract: Developing food products from local resources requires formulation strategies balancing ingredient incorporation with consumer acceptability while limiting experimental effort. This study investigated the formulation of a cassava-based biscuit containing Momordica charantia L. seed oil and press cake using consumer sensory evaluation and exploratory Bayesian optimization. A constrained mixture design generated 867 candidate formulations, reduced to 42. Five formulations were prepared and evaluated by 60 consumers using a seven-point hedonic scale. Friedman tests with Holm adjustment across five sensory attributes showed a significant difference only for texture (adjusted p = 2.82 × 10−5). Appearance, aroma, taste, and overall acceptability did not differ significantly. Texture was therefore retained for exploratory modelling. Responses for the 37 unevaluated formulations were estimated by inverse-distance weighting using three nearest neighbours. Combined with the five experimental measurements for kriging with a linear trend and a Matérn 3/2 covariance structure. An expected-improvement criterion identified a candidate formulation containing 35.08% cassava flour, 17.55% M. charantia press cake, 14.27% butter, 4.52% seed oil, and 14.02% sugar. Its predicted texture score was approximately 5.0–5.1. Combining consumer sensory evaluation with Bayesian modelling can help identify promising formulations of cassava-based biscuits. However, further experimental testing is needed to validate the predicted texture score.

papers.title: TPMS-based reformer for ammonia decomposition: Effect of Ni/Al2O3 catalyst thickness on heat and mass transfer for Schwarz-P topology
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures as a catalyst carrier are a perspective solution for compact reformers due to their high surface to volume ratio. In this work, the ammonia decomposition process is numerically investigated in a Schwarz-P TPMS-based reformer (10 mm unit cell) coated with a Ni / Al 2 O 3 catalyst. Catalyst layer thicknesses from 125 to 1000 μ m were analyzed across 623–923 K. The numerical predictions of ammonia conversion were validated against reference experimental data for a Ni / Al 2 O 3 catalyst from the references, demonstrating strong agreement with a mean absolute percentage deviation of less than 7%. The results show that catalyst layer thickness significantly influences reformer performance, particularly up to 500 μ m . However, further increases in thickness yield minimal improvements in ammonia decomposition process. This behavior indicates that for thicknesses greater than 500 μ m , the process becomes limited by internal mass transfer resistance, preventing the effective utilization of the additional catalyst volume.

papers.title: Energy Optimization and Decarbonization of Industrial Furnaces Through Hydrogen Hybridization and Predictive IoT Control
papers.abstract: Within the framework of Industry 4.0 and global decarbonization mandates, high-temperature thermal processes—such as industrial furnaces—represent one of the most challenging sectors to abate. Conventional combustion based on Natural Gas (NG) generates significant volumes of greenhouse gas (〖CO〗_2) emissions. Hydrogen (H_2) hybridization offers a direct pathway for thermal decarbonization; however, blending H_2 into combustion chambers introduces critical operational challenges, including thermal instability, variable flame propagation speeds, and a high risk of thermal 〖NO〗_x formation. Legacy reactive control architectures, such as PID loops, lack the predictive capabilities required to manage dynamic, non-linear fuel-mixture shifts. This paper designs and simulates an IoT-based Model Predictive Control (MPC) system deployed on an industrial Edge architecture to optimize energy efficiency and manage dynamic H_2/NGblending in industrial furnaces. The system requirements and user interface were structured using a user-centered Design Thinking methodology, while the core control logic was validated through a quantitative simulation model developed in Python/Simulink. Data acquisition relies on Modbus TCP and MQTT protocols, storing time-series telemetry in InfluxDB. A PRISMA 2020 systematic review of 20 recent studies (2018–2026) established the technical foundation. Simulation results demonstrate that a dynamic MPC controller operating at a 20% H_2volumetric ratio achieves a 6.8% direct reduction in 〖CO〗_2 emissions, maintains thermal stability within ±2.3∘C of setpoint, and suppresses 〖NO〗_x thermal spikes. Financial evaluation estimates a total implementation investment of MXN 185,000, yielding an Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 41.2% and a payback period of 1 year and 7 months. The findings confirm that software-driven IoT predictive control is a viable, high-impact solution for accelerating industrial thermal decarbonization.

papers.title: When Microsoft PowerPoint becomes a laboratory: building a semi-adaptive digital learning platform for inclusive microbiology education
papers.abstract: Laboratory-based microbiology education presents unique challenges for accessibility, flexibility and learner engagement. Students may require alternative pathways to access practical learning experiences due to disability, illness, placement commitments, geographic constraints, caring responsibilities, language barriers or differing learning preferences. While sophisticated adaptive learning platforms exist, they often require substantial institutional investment, technical expertise and ongoing support. This article describes a practical alternative: transforming Microsoft PowerPoint into a semi-adaptive digital laboratory learning platform that supports interactive, student-centred microbiology learning. Developed through the creative reconfiguration of familiar software, the platform combines authentic microbiological imagery, branching learning pathways, embedded feedback, videos and digital measurement tools to simulate key aspects of laboratory investigation. Drawing on literature surrounding active learning, adaptive learning, branching scenarios and inclusive educational design, the article outlines the pedagogical foundations, key design principles and implementation strategies for educators wishing to build their own semi-adaptive learning environments. The approach demonstrates how low-cost, readily available technologies can enhance learner autonomy, engagement, accessibility and flexibility while maintaining authentic microbiology learning experiences.

papers.title: Knowledge-guided supervisory architecture with an LLM-compatible interface for robust energy management of integrated storage under renewable uncertainty
papers.abstract: Introduction High renewable penetration couples forecast errors, storage dynamics, and grid constraints. We study a knowledge-guided supervisory architecture that maps operational context to bounded uncertainty margins, carbon and peak weights, degradation multipliers, and reserve targets. Methods A worst-corner rolling linear program coordinates battery, hydrogen, and thermal storage, followed by deterministic realized-balance repair. A large language model (LLM)-compatible interface is proposed, but the experiments use deterministic numeric context rules and do not execute retrieval, language-model inference, or a text parser. The synthetic 7-day comparison gives all model predictive control (MPC) controllers the same issued grid-event notices and emergency recourse. Results Each MPC controller achieves numerical zero unserved energy. Relative to fixed robust MPC, the adaptive supervisor decreases nominal peak import from 439.86 to 414.81 kW but increases evaluation cost from 3,160.73 to 3,337.12 USD and service-normalized emissions from 145.28 to 148.01 kg CO 2 /MWh. Four additional randomized scenarios show the same mean cost-peak trade-off, without establishing universal superiority. Isolated ablations and notice-recourse controls show that zero shortage is not unique to adaptive reasoning. All 57 released trajectories pass physical and accounting checks. Discussion Exact-projection and recursive-feasibility statements remain conditional theoretical results, not certificates for the implemented heuristic.

papers.title: Global Performance Optimization of an Internal Combustion Engine Using Surrogate-Based Optimization Modeling
papers.abstract: The automotive industry faces increasing regulatory pressure, driven by standards such as EU 2024/1257 and CONAMA No. 492. These guidelines require drastic reductions in emissions of nitrogen oxides (NOx), particulate matter, and greenhouse gases, which puts pressure on the development of cleaner engines. In this context, the calibration of the Engine Control Unit (ECU) has become a complex optimization challenge. Traditionally, calibration relied on extensive experimental testing on dynamometers. However, this method has become impractical due to the high financial cost and the long development time required. As an alternative, Model-Based Calibration (MBC) has emerged, enabling virtual exploration of the design space. Nevertheless, high-fidelity simulations of diesel combustion require a computational cost that is prohibitive for iterative optimization routines. Given this scenario, this work proposes a Surrogate-Based Optimization (SBO) framework applied to a real diesel engine. The methodology focuses on the analysis of six parameters: engine speed, intake pressure, injection timing, injection duration, injected fuel quantity, and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) mixture. The process uses the ANSYS CHEMKIN software to emulate engine behavior and generate high-fidelity data. Based on this dataset, a Neural Network is trained to act as a computationally inexpensive surrogate model. This model is integrated into an active learning cycle, where new conditions suggested by the optimization algorithm are validated by the physical simulator and reincorporated into the network’s training. Convergence of the process was achieved in only 252 engine cycles. The surrogate model presented a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of approximately 2% and coefficients of determination (R²) close to 1 for all variables. In the test case, the framework achieved an 11.70% reduction in fuel consumption and a 58.15% decrease in NOx emissions, at the cost of a slight reduction in power and torque.

papers.title: Development of a Portable 3D-Printed Fluorescence Imager for Student-Centered Learning in an Open-Lab Course
papers.abstract: Traditional fluorescence imagers, often bulky, expensive “black boxes”, limit student access to their internal optics and are impractical for resource-constrained educational settings. To address these pedagogical and practical barriers, we designed and fabricated a lightweight, portable fluorescence imaging device (≈300 g) integrated with a smartphone. All core components including the dark box, optical module holder, sample positioning area, and imaging area were fully 3D printed, keeping total material costs below \$40. Using fluorescent microneedle (MN) arrays as the imaging target, we optimized camera parameters and placed the MN patch in the illumination chamber. Image acquisition is typically completed within 1 min, enabling precise quantification of color and intensity. The study also evaluated the effects of ambient temperature and lighting on MN imaging. Notably, the device features an adjustable MN holder that allows imaging angles to be flexibly set between 10° and 30°. This low-cost, open-design platform provides an accessible hands-on tool for real-time fluorescence observation and analysis, making it a viable and economical option for institutions with limited equipment budgets to expand hands-on access to optical instrumentation. More importantly, the device was embedded within an inquiry-based laboratory course that engaged students in an iterative process of equipment assembly, optimization, and application. Through this course, students achieved a deeper conceptual understanding of fluorescence imaging principles, gained practical experience in experimental design and data quantification, and strengthened their collaborative problem-solving skills. The project thus demonstrates how affordable, student-built instrumentation can transform traditional laboratories into active learning environments that foster both technical competency and scientific inquiry.

papers.title: Medium-Dependent Swelling Response and Biological Performance of Methacrylated Chitosan Hydrogels Functionalized with Lanthanum Oxide Nanoparticles and Copper Tripeptide
papers.abstract: Methacrylated chitosan hydrogels are promising multifunctional materials for extrusion-based 3D bioprinting and may provide a platform for the future development of stimuli-responsive 4D biofabrication systems. This study evaluated chitosan-based hydrogel formulations prepared at different pH values and functionalized with lanthanum oxide nanoparticles and a copper tripeptide. The materials were characterized by swelling tests in water, PBS, SBF, and acidic medium, UV–Vis spectroscopy, FT-IR analysis, preliminary extrusion-printing tests, enzymatic biodegradation, DPPH radical scavenging, antibacterial testing against Escherichia coli, and XTT cytotoxicity assessment using 1321N1 cells. The hydrogels exhibited pronounced medium-dependent swelling, with a particularly strong initial response under acidic conditions, consistent with protonation of residual amino groups in the chitosan matrix. Preliminary printing experiments demonstrated continuous extrusion and stable filament formation, while FT-IR analysis and macroscopic observations supported successful photocrosslinking. The modified hydrogels showed antibacterial and antioxidant activity, substantial enzymatic degradability, and generally acceptable cytocompatibility, although the formulation with the highest additive content at the lowest preparation pH reduced cell viability below 70%. Overall, the developed materials represent multifunctional, extrusion-processable and photocrosslinkable hydrogel candidates for 3D bioprinting. Their stimulus-sensitive swelling behavior additionally supports further investigation for future 4D biofabrication, although programmed post-printing shape transformation was not evaluated in the present study.

papers.title: Thermo-Geometric Interpretation of Build Orientation and Strut Size on the Microstructure and Mechanical Behaviour of LPBF-Fabricated Ti–6Al–4V BCC Lattice Structures
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) was used to fabricate stress-relieved Ti–6Al–4V extra-low interstitial (ELI) body-centred cubic (BCC) lattice structures with nominal strut diameters of 1.0 and 1.5 mm in horizontal and vertical build orientations. The study combines scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Vickers microhardness testing, and compression testing to describe orientation and geometry associated differences. Mean measured strut diameters were 0.93 and 1.42 mm, corresponding to deviations of −7% and approximately −5%, respectively. The retained orientation level compression summaries report higher compressive strength and yield strength for vertical builds (324.1 and 171.6 MPa) than horizontal builds (248.0 and 156.0 MPa), while the reported elastic modulus is lower for vertical builds (2.5 GPa versus 4.3 GPa). Condition-level hardness values ranged from 310.40 ± 15.10 HV1 (horizontal, 1.0 mm) to 317.83 ± 23.29 HV1 (vertical, 1.5 mm). XRD intensity ratios are treated as semi-quantitative, and EBSD results are limited to the measured maps and morphology/orientation features; neither method, as retained here, establishes absolute α′ fractions or reconstructed prior-β grain alignment. Because specimen level compression data and numerical density records are incomplete, all mechanical comparisons are descriptive. Thermal explanations are qualitative hypotheses rather than validated measurements or simulations.

papers.title: Projection and uncertainty quantification of global hydrological drought from a non-stationary perspective
papers.abstract: Comprehensive projections and uncertainty quantification of global hydrological drought from a non-stationary perspective remain limited. To address this issue, we develop a time-varying threshold level (TLvar) method within a deconstruct-reshape framework to assess non-stationary hydrological drought. We apply the TLvar method to a multi-model experiment covering six global hydrological models (GHMs) driven by five bias-corrected global climate models (GCMs) under three shared socio-economic pathways (SSPs). Comparison with the traditional time-invariant threshold method shows that the TLvar method better characterizes non-stationary drought processes and more effectively captures the increasing trend in projected drought areas. Projections via the TLvar method show that global hydrological drought deficit will rise by 8.78% (SSP1-2.6) to 16.50% (SSP5-8.5) at the end of the 21st century (2071–2100) relative to the historical reference period (1985–2014), while hydrological drought duration is expected to stay unchanged across the three scenarios. The interaction between GHM and GCM is the dominant uncertainty source for projected changes in hydrological drought characteristics. Overall, the proposed TLvar method and its application to different GHM-GCM-SSP combinations could provide a valuable understanding of future hydrological drought changes under non-stationary conditions.

papers.title: Anodised Aluminium Surface Characterisation for Cooling of High-Performance Electronic Components
papers.abstract: Efficient heat dissipation is essential for high-performance electronic components. This study investigates the effects of sulfuric acid anodisation on the morphology, roughness, and wettability of Al 1050 surfaces, together with a preliminary assessment of water pool boiling performance. Samples were anodised for 10–60 min and characterised using scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, profilometry, and static contact angle measurements. Among the quantitatively characterised conditions, S40 exhibited the highest mean oxide thickness and surface pore opening fraction, whereas S50 exhibited the highest mean pore diameter. Anodisation increased surface roughness and reduced water contact angles, with S50 showing the lowest mean contact angle among the measured conditions. Preliminary boiling experiments comparing S0 and S50 showed similar power-dependent trends in apparent heat transfer coefficient. However, incomplete uncertainty quantification prevented a definitive assessment of thermal enhancement. Changes in nucleation behaviour, bubble detachment, and coating thermal resistance remain possible explanations rather than experimentally established mechanisms. S40 was not tested under boiling conditions; therefore, its thermal performance and the optimum anodisation duration for boiling remain unresolved. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of anodised surfaces and future combinations with spatially controlled surface texturing.

papers.title: Fixed point theorems for generalized contractions in super metric spaces with applications to neural computing
papers.abstract: The study of fixed point (FP) theorems within generalized distance structures continues to provide a powerful analytical foundation for nonlinear models and iterative learning systems. In this paper, we extend classical contraction principles to the framework of complete super metric spaces (CSMS) by introducing and analyzing several new contractive conditions. We first establish an extended max-type contraction theorem, followed by Kannan-type and Chatterjea-type results adapted to the super metric environment. Furthermore, we develop a neural contraction mapping theorem, offering a rigorous connection between FP theory and the stability of neural operator models, recurrent networks, and iterative training schemes. The derived conditions guarantee the existence and uniqueness of stable equilibria in nonlinear and neural mappings. Illustrative examples demonstrate the applicability of these results to both analytical and computational systems, thereby bridging the gap between abstract FP theory and modern neural computation.

papers.title: Automating the ETL Pipeline: Machine Learning Approaches to Data Cleaning and Integration
papers.abstract: Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) pipelines remain the backbone of enterprise analytics, yet the transformation stage, and in particular data cleaning and data integration, is still dominated by hand-written rules, brittle scripts and expensive manual review. Practitioners commonly report that preparing data consumes far more effort than analysing it, and that errors introduced at this stage propagate silently into dashboards, reports and machine learning models. This research presents AutoETL, a modular machine learning framework that automates error detection, value repair, schema matching and entity resolution inside a single orchestrated pipeline. The framework borrows the Quality-by-Design (QbD) mindset from pharmaceutical development by defining a Quality Target Product Profile (QTPP) and Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) for the curated output, and by controlling the pipeline through a measurable design space and control plan. Error detection combines Isolation Forest anomaly scores with a gradient-boosted classifier trained by uncertainty-driven active learning under a budget of only 100 labelled tuples; repair relies on chained gradient-boosted imputers; schema matching blends embedding, lexical and type similarity through the Hungarian algorithm; and entity resolution couples locality-sensitive-hashing blocking with an XGBoost pair classifier. Experiments on three cleaning benchmarks (Hospital, Flights, Beers), three entity-resolution benchmarks (Abt-Buy, Amazon-Google, DBLP-ACM) and a synthetic enterprise workload of up to ten million records show a mean detection F1-score of 0.88, a normalised imputation error of 0.221, a mean match F1-score of 0.81 and near-linear scalability, while Population Stability Index monitoring keeps quality stable over time. Paired significance tests (p < 0.01) confirm that the improvements over rule-based, ensemble and neural baselines are statistically reliable.

papers.title: Efektivitas Model Active Learning dalam Pembelajaran Pendidikan Jasmani terhadap Aktivitas Fisik Sedang hingga Berat, Kompetensi Gerak, dan Motivasi Belajar Siswa Sekolah Dasar
papers.abstract: Physical education (PJOK) in elementary schools is still largely teacher-centered, which limits students' movement time. This study examined the effect of an Active Learning Model on moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), movement competence, and learning motivation of elementary school students. A quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design involved 80 fifth-grade students at SD Inpres Karunrung, Makassar (experimental n = 40; control n = 40). The experimental group received 36 sessions (12 weeks) of Active Learning Model instruction, while the control group received conventional PJOK instruction with the same time allocation. MVPA was measured with the System for Observing Fitness Instruction Time (SOFIT), movement competence with the Canadian Agility and Movement Skill Assessment (CAMSA), and motivation with the Physical Education Motivation Scale (PEMS). Data were analyzed with a 2 × 2 mixed ANOVA. The group × time interaction was significant for MVPA (F(1, 78) = 61.24; ηp² = 0.440), movement competence (F(1, 78) = 39.86; ηp² = 0.338), and learning motivation (F(1, 78) = 46.52; ηp² = 0.374), all p < 0.001. The experimental group improved more than the control group on all three outcomes. The Active Learning Model may improve the quality of elementary PJOK, although the quasi-experimental design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Digital Testing of Capability Boundaries for Low-RCS Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Under Radar Detection
papers.abstract: Capability boundaries of low-RCS unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are difficult to map through flight testing alone. This study presents a threshold-guided digital-testing workflow that connects aerodynamic-model construction, flight-response calibration, and sequential boundary search for a high-speed, low-observable UAV operating against a generic ground-based surveillance radar. A multi-source, multi-fidelity surrogate reduces the computational burden of the selected aerodynamic-database allocation, sequential least-squares quadratic programming calibrates the flight-response model, and Latin hypercube sampling, factor screening, Kriging surfaces, and Bayesian optimization organize the search for task windows. Three tasks are considered: low-response flight, response-reduction maneuvering, and active-emission response mapping. The first and third tasks use a case-level radar-response index P rather than a binomial detection probability, whereas the second uses a paired response-reduction metric U. The results support three engineering observations within the stated model domain. Flight-path offset is the primary screening variable for low-response flight and guides subsequent refinement of the altitude-detection-range boundary. Commanded heading is the dominant factor of the tested climb-plus-yaw maneuver, with headings above 150 degrees associated with a response reduction exceeding 15% under the fixed reference condition. Smaller offsets and larger emission-gain settings define the principal high-response region in the active-emission scenario. The practical contribution is a structured procedure for converting sparse simulation outputs into candidate route, maneuver, and emission settings. The numerical windows are model-conditional and are not universal radar-performance limits. The same threshold-guided organization may also support civilian flight-safety assessment and aerodynamic-envelope testing when appropriately validated safety metrics are used.

papers.title: Weak Sparse Identification for Van der Pol Control and BLDC‐Driven Double‐Pendulum Reconstruction
papers.abstract: We evaluate weak sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (WSINDy) in two settings: simulated control of a Van der Pol oscillator and experimental reconstruction of a brushless direct‐current (BLDC)‐driven planar double pendulum. On the nondimensional Van der Pol benchmark, the total open‐loop state root‐mean‐square error (RMSE) decreases from 0.57 for an unfiltered finite‐difference sparse‐identification baseline to 0.26 for the implemented WSINDy pipeline. Controllers based on the learned model achieve tracking RMSEs of 0.31 with feedback‐linearization‐inspired inversion and 0.28 with real‐time iteration model predictive control (RTI‐MPC). In the experiment, the robot's upper body is rigidly fixed so that one hip‐knee leg moves without ground contact as a double pendulum with two degrees of freedom. Using measured motor currents, WSINDy reconstructs the measured hip and knee rotation angles on the identification record with RMSEs of and rad, respectively. The acceleration comparison is strongly affected by finite‐difference amplification of measurement noise, so it cannot be used on its own to isolate unmodeled physics. Experimental closed‐loop control, ground‐contact impacts, and gait‐level switching remain outside the scope of the present study.

papers.title: Machine learning for ionospheric scintillation: detection, characterization and prediction
papers.abstract: Ionospheric scintillation refers to rapid amplitude and phase fluctuations of radio signals caused by electron density irregularities, which can severely degrade the performance of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) and satellite communications. Existing reviews focus on empirical climatological and physics-based propagation models, or survey machine learning (ML) for general ionospheric parameters such as total electron content and geomagnetic indices. In this review, we systematically summarize the recent progress in ML for ionospheric scintillation around three tasks, namely detection, characterization, and prediction, and we use a general input-output mapping framework that covers both single-station and regional scenarios, and integrates conventional methods and data-driven models. For detection, we show how ML replaces fixed thresholds with data-driven nonlinear decision boundaries. For characterization, we review how ML estimates irregularity intensity, spatial structure, and drift in F-region equatorial plasma bubbles and traveling ionospheric disturbances, as well as mid-latitude sporadic-E layers governed by distinct mechanisms. For prediction, we trace progress from single-station short-term forecasts to regional spatiotemporal field reconstruction, separate climatological occurrence probabilities from the prediction of individual events, and synthesize the available uncertainty quantification and probabilistic forecasting methods together with their validation. Looking forward, we identify physically consistent drivers, the integration of ionospheric mechanisms into ML models, leakage-free cross-station and cross-year validation, and calibrated probabilistic forecasts as the priorities that will move ML from retrospective analysis toward the trustworthy operational space-weather service.

papers.title: Forecasting ENSO ‐Effect on Extreme Hot Days in Vietnam With Climate‐Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: A fundamental assumption in many applied machine learning studies is that a single predictive model can be universally adopted across diverse spatial domains. This study challenges the ‘one‐model‐fits‐all’ paradigm in the context of extreme hot‐day forecasting across 48 meteorological stations in Vietnam using 41 years of historical data (1981–2021). By benchmarking five advanced predictive architectures (XGBoost, LSTM, TCN, NHiTS and TFT) driven by local meteorology and large‐scale climate indices, we demonstrate that no single model is statistically superior across all regions. This statistical parity emphasizes that predictive performance is inherently location‐dependent due to spatial climate heterogeneity, necessitating an adaptive station‐wise model selection framework to maximize local accuracy. Furthermore, the predictive capabilities of these five ML/DL architectures were rigorously benchmarked against three reference models (Damped Anomaly Persistence, Rolling Climatology and Expanding Climatology), demonstrating substantial predictive improvements with positive skill scores across the climatic regions. In addition, operational climate services require more than deterministic accuracy. They also demand transparent and trustworthy risk communication. Consequently, we propose a forecasting framework that integrates three complementary components: (1) adaptive station‐wise model selection, (2) baseline uncertainty quantification via split conformal prediction targeting 90% nominal coverage, and (3) explainable artificial intelligence (SHAP and fANOVA) for climate‐driver attribution and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis. Although the framework achieved an empirical global coverage of approximately 87%, we identified critical reliability degradations driven by asymmetric upper‐tail misses during extremely hot months, transitional climate phases, and specific climate extremes (e.g., QBO and PNA). Ultimately, this research demonstrates that predicting hydro‐meteorological extremes requires shifting from global point‐forecasting to adaptive model selection coupled with explicit climate‐conditional uncertainty characterization and interpretable feature attribution.

papers.title: Surrogate-assisted GA–PSO optimization of Bi-directionally functionally graded TPMS sandwich plates based on linear buckling performance with nonlinear post-buckling assessment
papers.abstract: Sandwich plates constructed with triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattice cores and composite face sheets deliver outstanding specific stiffness, yet the coupled effect of in-plane bidirectional functional grading and edge restraints on buckling has not been systematically quantified. This study proposes an integrated simulation optimization framework to fill that gap. Nine TPMS architectures belonging to the Primitive, Primary IWP, and Secondary IWP families are parametrically generated. A two-directional power-law distribution with exponent n a, n b ∈ [0.5, 5] is applied along both the length and width axes, arranged in four bi-grading patterns: symmetric–symmetric (SS), symmetric–asymmetric (SA), asymmetric–symmetric (AS), and asymmetric–asymmetric (AA). Four sets of boundary conditions CFCF, SFSF, CSCS, and SSSS are considered. The linear buckling load per unit mass is evaluated for all configurations using a Chebyshev–Ritz approach. To construct a continuous predictive model, an AdaBoost ensemble of regression is trained (DWKNN, ELM, MLP, SVR), iteratively enhancing weak learners to precisely capture the linear buckling-to-weight landscape. A hybrid genetic algorithm–particle swarm optimization (GA–PSO) routine then interrogates the surrogate to extract the optimal grading exponents. At the located optima, nonlinear post-buckling equilibrium paths are computed through an arc-length technique, with the structural formulation grounded in first-order shear deformation theory and nonlinear von Kármán. Results demonstrate that the SS material arrangement raises the mass-specific buckling capacity compared to a uniform core baseline without any mass penalty, delivering the highest resistance in both linear and nonlinear regimes. The presented tool constitutes a generalizable design methodology and conclusively establishes bi-symmetric functional grading as the most effective strategy for buckling enhancement in TPMS-cored sandwich plates.

papers.title: Automated Standardization of Companion Diagnostics Using Deep Learning: Claudin18.2 as a Paradigm in Gastric Cancer
papers.abstract: Companion diagnostic biomarkers are essential for selecting patients for targeted and immunotherapeutic intervention. However, their clinical implementation is frequently limited by analytical reproducibility, inter‐observer variability, and clone‐dependent interpretation in immunohistochemistry (IHC) assays. Claudin18.2, an emerging biomarker in gastric cancer, exemplifies these challenges. We developed an end‐to‐end, deep learning–driven pipeline augmented with active learning for automated and quantitative assessment of IHC‐stained whole‐slide images (WSIs). Using Claudin18.2 as a representative biomarker, the model was trained on 43‐14A clone and validated in both retrospective and prospective gastric cancer cohorts. Generalizability across alternative antibody clones was assessed, and the model's capacity for cross‐clone concordance analysis was investigated. The model demonstrated almost perfect agreement with the pathologist‐defined reference standard for 2/3+ staining (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.849 and 0.894) and robust classification performance across clinically relevant thresholds (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.764–0.828 and 0.865–0.904), matching or surpassing pathologists’ evaluation while improving efficiency. Importantly, the pipeline maintained strong performance in cross‐clone analyses, supporting clone‐independent application. This scalable AI framework enables standardized, quantitative, and cross‐clone interpretation of Claudin18.2 IHC; the approach has the potential to enhance the precision, reproducibility, and accessibility of biomarker‐driven patient selection in routine clinical practice.

papers.title: A Review of Machine Learning-Enhanced Monte Carlo Methods for Financial Risk Management
papers.abstract: Monte Carlo simulation has been a standard tool in financial risk management for decades, yet it converges slowly and becomes expensive when models are high-dimensional, when risk must be measured in real time, or when extreme market states matter. Machine learning has entered this workflow in three main ways. Deep importance sampling trains a neural network to learn the measure change that makes rare tail events more likely under the sampler, so the variance of value-at-risk estimates drops sharply for a fixed number of paths. Generative models, Quant GANs among them, synthesize extreme yet plausible market states; because the synthetic paths reproduce heavy tails and volatility clustering, they ease the chronic shortage of tail data. A third line replaces expensive pricing or loss computations with a trained neural surrogate that answers within milliseconds, a good fit for tasks that need repeated valuation. This study reviews the methods behind these three lines and their applications, including value-at-risk and expected shortfall estimation, stress scenario generation, credit portfolio loss simulation, and deep hedging. It also weighs the open problems. Black-box models remain difficult to explain to regulators under FRTB, tail regions are data-poor, and no accepted validation standard has emerged. This study concludes by arguing for Bayesian uncertainty quantification inside the simulation loop, validation procedures that regulators can accept, and evaluation frameworks that price the new model risk.

papers.abstract: This study investigates model predictive control (MPC) of a multirotor drone (unmanned aerial vehicle, UAV) carrying a cable-suspended payload, comparing conventional shifted initialization with Transformer-based warm starting of a sequential convex programming (SCP) optimizer. The controller uses a coupled mechanical model with an elastic cable and a double-pendulum representation of the suspended load. Its formulation includes move-blocked control inputs, finite-difference sensitivities, constrained quadratic subproblems, and input-feasibility projection. A Transformer trained on expert SCP solutions predicts an initial control sequence, which is subsequently refined by the same optimizer used for the conventional methods. Numerical experiments compare zero, shifted, and Transformer initialization under identical controller settings. For independently solved MPC problems, Transformer initialization reduces computation time relative to zero initialization. In sequential closed-loop simulations, however, shifting the preceding optimized control sequence provides the lowest computation time, while all three methods produce similar tracking behavior. These findings emphasize the importance of comparing learned warm starts with conventional initialization methods that reuse previous MPC solutions. The measured optimization times exceed the control sampling period; consequently, real-time implementation is not demonstrated.   Keywords: Model predictive control; sequential convex programming; Transformer; warm start; cable-suspended payload; multirotor drone.

papers.title: Data-free continuous-time physics-informed neural networks for vortex shedding: a consistent pressure across time windows
papers.abstract: Without data, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in continuous time have so far failed to develop vortex shedding past a circular cylinder in a domain symmetric about the wake centerline: the training converges to the steady symmetric solution. We obtain shedding at Re=100 with a continuous-time PINN trained over successive time windows, without any reference data and without temporal discretization, the symmetry being broken by an analytical, divergence-free initial condition. The Strouhal number and the mean drag coefficient agree with an OpenFOAM solution computed on the same domain to within 0.5%. The pressure, however, is discontinuous at the junctions between windows, and the lift coefficient is a staircase. We relate this discontinuity to the differential-algebraic structure of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, of index 2 after spatial discretization: a consistent initial condition of each window must satisfy the constraint $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}=0$ for the velocity, and the hidden constraint $\nabla\cdot\partial_t\mathbf{v}=0$, with $\partial_t\mathbf{v}$ given by the momentum equation, then determines the pressure. Imposing the pressure alone makes the solution continuous but not consistent; our remedy imposes the pressure at the junctions and adds this hidden constraint to the loss. Over five shedding periods, the jumps of the lift coefficient become 20 times smaller.

papers.title: SplatWAM: Splatting World Action Models for Real-Time 3D Imagination
papers.abstract: World models typically predict future observations in pixel or latent space, limiting their ability to directly represent true 3D scene evolution. We present SplatWAM (Splatting World Action Model), a generative world model that learns action-conditioned dynamics directly over compact 3D Gaussian primitives. A tokenizer SplatWAM-T first encodes a variable number of unposed views into a fixed budget of Gaussian tokens. A dynamics model SplatWAM-D then predicts future Gaussian states in a single forward pass per action, using log-Euclidean covariance coordinates and differentiable rendering supervision to facilitate learning in an explicit 3D space. Each predicted state can be rasterized from arbitrary viewpoints, enforcing a shared 3D representation across views by construction. On OGBench Scene, SplatWAM renders novel views 12x faster than video world models (~80 FPS on an RTX 5090) with up to 2.0 dB higher PSNR. We further introduce SplatWAM-P, a lightweight flow-matching policy head jointly trained with the dynamics model. Across 8 task suites, model-free Gaussian-token policies outperform pixel-based counterparts by up to 24.8 percentage points. SplatWAM-P improves over Latent Particle World Model (LPWM) by 12 percentage points and matches HIQL without a learned value function. On LIBERO, our ~1B model outperforms WorldVLA (~7B) and the robot-pretrained OpenVLA (~7B), while matching OpenVLA-OFT when both are trained without large-scale robot pretraining. Code and checkpoints will be released.

SuperMimic trains a tracking policy by backpropagating through the rollouts of a learned world model. We extend it to MS-Human-700 (700 muscles) and MyoFullBody (354 muscles), with MuJoCo's activation dynamics inside the world model. To make its training fast, our recipe takes the speedups developed for the Unitree G1, replaces three of their settings that fail on muscles, and adds four changes of our own: observations without muscle geometry, data collection concurrent with the updates, Beta exploration noise that keeps every excitation in $[0,1]$, and 50 Hz control. On one RTX 5090 it trains MS-Human-700 in 6.3 minutes to the held-out return that SuperMimic's published hyperparameters reach in 3.9 hours, 37$\times$ sooner, and in 20 minutes to lower tracking errors than theirs after 10 hours. It trains MyoFullBody 34$\times$ sooner without retuning. Ablations show what is specific to muscles: a higher policy learning rate stalls half of the runs, and clipped Gaussian noise adds a tonic co-contraction that Beta noise avoids. Finally, refining the policy's actions through the world model at test time lowers the position error by a further 26% with no held-out clip failing, and reaches the same return after 5.1 instead of 6.3 minutes of training. Code, the training recipe and videos are on the project page https://muscle-supermimic.beanpow.top.

papers.title: Federated Learning with Uncertainty Quantification on Pseudo Label Exchange
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate federated stochastic operator learning for stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), with an emphasis on heterogeneous client data distributions and uncertainty quantification. Federated learning enables clients to collaboratively train models without exchanging their original solution data, but conventional federated averaging can suffer significant performance degradation when client distributions differ, particularly when their input function supports are disjoint. To address these challenges, we propose the Federated Stochastic Operator Network (FedSON), a two-phase framework that combines auxiliary data construction with stochastic operator learning. In the first phase, locally trained deterministic neural operators and their corresponding input functions are exchanged to generate pseudolabeled auxiliary data, enabling the federated model to learn across heterogeneous input distributions without sharing original solution trajectories. In the second phase, a stochastic operator network is trained on top of the frozen deterministic operator to characterize stochastic fluctuations and quantify uncertainty in the predicted solutions. Numerical experiments involving the heat equation, viscous Burgers' equation, and two-dimensional advection-diffusion equation demonstrate the FedSON substantially improves deterministic prediction accuracy under heterogeneous client distributions while producing uncertainty estimates comparable to those obtained through centralized training.

papers.title: FOCI: Trajectory Optimization on Gaussian Splats for Gaussian Robots
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently gained popularity as a faster alternative to Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) in 3D reconstruction and view synthesis methods. Leveraging the spatial information encoded in 3DGS, this work proposes FOCI (Field Overlap Collision Integral), an algorithm that is able to optimize trajectories directly on the Gaussians themselves. FOCI leverages a novel and interpretable collision formulation for 3DGS using the notion of the overlap integral between Gaussians. The formulation presented applies to different robot morphologies (e.g., fixed and mobile base manipulators, legged robots, UAVs) and handles both static and dynamic Gaussian-Splat environments. Contrary to other approaches, which represent the robot with conservative bounding boxes that underestimate the traversability of the environment, we propose to represent the environment and the robot as Gaussian Splats. This not only has desirable computational properties, but also allows for orientation-aware planning, allowing the robot to pass through very tight and narrow spaces. We extensively test our algorithm in both synthetic and real Gaussian Splats, showcasing that collision-free trajectories for legged, aerial and manipulator robots can be computed in seconds, even with hundreds of thousands of Gaussians making up the environment. The code is available at https://github.com/leggedrobotics/foci

papers.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning for Total Kinetic Energy Distributions in Neutron-Induced Fission
papers.abstract: The incident-neutron-energy dependence of post-neutron total-kinetic-energy (TKE) distributions, particularly their width in the multichance-fission regime, provides a sensitive test of fission calculations. We investigate how the General Description of Fission Observables (GEF) and probabilistic machine-learning models trained on GEF reproduce measured TKE distributions, emphasizing their width at high incident-neutron energies and extrapolation beyond the training range. Gaussian process regression (GPR), GPR with a white-noise kernel, a mixture density network (MDN), and a Bayesian mixture density network (BMDN) are evaluated on a common calculated dataset. An extended MDN/BMDN analysis uses 1,025 GEF spectra from 20 target nuclei and 60 measured distributions. Training ranges of up to 20, 40, and approximately 76 MeV are compared with matched-size controls extending to 30 or 40 MeV while preserving the number of spectra per target. Above 40 MeV, the BMDN width mean absolute error relative to experiment decreases from 5.63 MeV for training up to 20 MeV to 2.70 and 2.53 MeV for two matched-size 30-MeV controls and 1.77 MeV for the matched-size 40-MeV control. Predictive-interval coverage relative to GEF above 40 MeV rises from 52.3% to 92.3% between the 20-MeV and full training ranges. Agreement with measured mean TKE and widths is target dependent, with no uniform ordering among GEF, MDN, and BMDN. The results demonstrate the sensitivity of high-energy widths to training-energy coverage, with improvements already evident at 30 MeV. The comparatively slow variation of GEF widths at high energies limits the extent to which these improvements can be attributed to learning nontrivial energy dependence. Adequate training-energy coverage is critical for reproducing the calculated high-energy evolution, while agreement with experiment remains constrained by the underlying fission model.

papers.title: FlowersBench: A FluidFlower-Inspired Dataset for Benchmarking Carbon Storage Surrogates Across Geological Structures
papers.abstract: Machine learning surrogates are emerging as a computationally efficient tool for uncertainty quantification in geological carbon storage (GCS). Geological structure constitutes a major source of uncertainty; however, existing benchmark simulation datasets predominantly vary petrophysical and operational parameters within a fixed geological setting. Generalisation to unseen geological structures therefore remains largely unexplored. We introduce FlowersBench, a benchmark dataset of 5,000 two-dimensional, reservoir-scale CO$_2$ storage simulations across 244 structural geometries. The geometries are sampled from an in-house structural generator inspired by the FluidFlower experiments and Case B of the 11th Society of Petroleum Engineers Comparative Solution Project (SPE11B). Each simulation is run with Open Porous Media (OPM) Flow over a 50-year injection period and a 500-year post-injection monitoring period. Test geometries are withheld from training to assess generalisation to unseen structural geometries. Two additional subsets support evaluation under structural shift. The first extends the parameter ranges of the structural generator beyond those used for training, and the second introduces an unseen topology of multiple parallel faults. A baseline U-Net surrogate is trained to predict CO$_2$ gas saturation. In representative test cases, the surrogate recovers the main migration pathways, including lateral spreading beneath low-permeability layers and upward flow along fault damage zones, with errors concentrated near the plume boundary. Under both structural shifts, prediction error exceeds that on the held-out geometries, and the increase in relative error is greater for the unseen fault topology. FlowersBench is publicly available and provides a common basis for evaluating GCS surrogates across geological structures.
