papers.title: MonoQPM: Splitting Features into Concepts for Inherent Interpretability and Predictive Performance
papers.abstract: Alongside superposition, polysemanticity is one of the primary obstacles to achieving interpretable deep neural networks. While these phenomena are typically intrinsically linked, the Quadratic Programming Enhanced Model (QPM) naturally decouples them. By representing classes with a sparse binary assignment of very few features, QPM prevents superposition by design on its final features but still exhibits polysemanticity. However, measuring polysemanticity is an open problem. This work proposes a utility-focused approach to measuring polysemanticity by quantifying the decrease in interference-induced activation errors, which yields the practical utility of tighter prediction sets using Conformal Prediction (CP). We explicitly disentangle the polysemantic features of QPM into monosemantic concepts to create the Monosemantic QPM (MonoQPM). Because its features are disentangled, MonoQPM acts as a significantly more efficient Conformal Predictor. Additionally, we introduce CUBCars, a dataset providing ground truth information about shared concepts. Using this and other datasets, we demonstrate that polysemanticity emerges in QPM across all tested architectures, but is effectively alleviated by MonoQPM. For instance, MonoQPM guarantees 88% coverage using Adaptive Prediction Sets on ImageNet with just 66% of the frozen QPM's set size.

papers.title: From Sustainable Extraction to Functional Bioinks: Seaweed-Derived Polysaccharides for 3D/4D Bioprinting and Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Seaweed-derived polysaccharides are emerging as renewable and biocompatible biomaterials for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, wound healing, drug delivery, and advanced biofabrication. Their performance is governed by interconnected factors, including extraction and purification, molecular architecture, molecular weight, sulfation, uronic acid composition, rheology, gelation, crosslinking behavior, and biological interactions. However, these determinants are often considered separately, obscuring how upstream processing influences downstream functionality. This review integrates sustainable polysaccharide recovery with structural characterization, hydrogel engineering, bioink formulation, 3D/4D bioprinting, and biomedical performance. Emphasis is placed on alginate, carrageenan, fucoidan, ulvan, agarose, and laminarin, highlighting structure–property–function relationships relevant to functional biomaterials. Emerging extraction and fractionation strategies, including enzyme-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, microwave-assisted, subcritical-water, and deep eutectic solvent-based processes, are critically evaluated with respect to polymer integrity, purity, and biofabrication performance. Key physicochemical attributes are further linked to printability, shape fidelity, mechanical stability, cell compatibility, and biological function, providing a framework for rational bioink design and selection. The review also examines the transition from conventional 3D bioprinting to stimuli-responsive 4D biofabrication, where seaweed-derived polymers can be engineered into dynamic bioinks responsive to physiological or external cues. Current challenges, including compositional variability, purification, mechanical limitations, sterilization, reproducibility, standardization, scalability, and regulatory translation, are critically assessed. Future priorities for integrating sustainable processing, molecular characterization, bioink design, and translational validation are outlined to accelerate the development of clinically relevant, scalable, and environmentally sustainable marine biomaterials. This integrated perspective connects marine-resource processing with next-generation biofabrication and defines key directions for translating seaweed polysaccharides from laboratory materials to biomedical technologies.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Printing and Regenerative Medicine in Biomedical Engineering: A Bibliometric and Systematic Review of Emerging Trends, Biomaterials, and Clinical Translation
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing has become an important enabling technology in regenerative medicine, supporting the development of biomaterials, tissue-engineered constructs, and patient-specific biomedical solutions. However, the rapid expansion of the literature has created a need for integrated assessments of research trends, technological developments, and translational challenges. This study presents a combined bibliometric and systematic review of research on 3D printing, regenerative medicine, and biomedical engineering using the Scopus database. Bibliometric analyses evaluated publication growth, subject-area distribution, keyword co-occurrence patterns, geographical contributions, funding sponsors, and leading publication sources. In parallel, a PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted to examine studies published between 2022 and 2026. From an initial dataset of 456 records, 51 publications met the eligibility criteria and were classified into five thematic categories: bioprinting and biofabrication technologies, biomedical and clinical applications, biomaterials and bioink development, tissue engineering scaffolds, regenerative constructs, and review articles and evidence-synthesis studies. Bibliometric results showed that research activity is primarily concentrated in engineering, materials science, and biochemistry, with the United States, India, and China representing the most productive countries. The systematic review identified recurring research priorities related to multifunctional biomaterials, advanced biofabrication strategies, vascularized tissue models, process optimization, and artificial intelligence-assisted manufacturing. Across the reviewed studies, vascularization, manufacturing reproducibility, standardization, scalability, and clinical translation emerged as the most frequently reported barriers to implementation. The findings demonstrate increasing integration between materials engineering, biofabrication technologies, and biological functionality, highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of the field. Future progress will depend on advances in standardized manufacturing workflows, vascularized tissue engineering, data-driven process control, and clinically translatable regenerative systems.

papers.title: A Critical Review of Fatigue Behavior in WAAM‐CMT and SLM 316L Stainless Steel
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing enables complex 316L stainless steel components; however, fatigue performance depends on manufacturing characteristics and testing conditions. This review compares the fatigue behavior of 316L stainless steel produced by wire arc additive manufacturing using cold metal transfer (WAAM‐CMT) and selective laser melting (SLM). The analysis covers fatigue strength and life, crack initiation and propagation, surface condition, defects, microstructure, residual stresses, and post‐processing. The literature indicates that surface roughness, defects, and microstructural heterogeneity influence fatigue performance. SLM specimens show favorable high‐cycle fatigue performance, whereas some report greater crack‐growth resistance for WAAM‐produced material. These differences reflect distinct fatigue mechanisms. Direct comparisons remain challenging because of variations in testing conditions, specimen geometries, and fatigue‐limit definitions. Post‐processing can improve fatigue performance depending on the treatment and initial material condition. This review identifies key factors and research gaps, emphasizing standardized testing and reporting for reliable comparisons between WAAM‐CMT and SLM 316L stainless steel.

papers.title: Hybrid 3D Biofabrication Using a Combination of an In Situ Mechanical Fiber Spinning Method and Extrusion‐Based 3D (Bio) Printing for Skeletal Muscle Tissue Engineering Applications
papers.abstract: This work presents a hybrid biofabrication strategy for skeletal muscle tissue engineering applications. This is achieved by the true integration of 3D (bio) printing (3DBP) of an alginate‐carboxymethyl cellulose (SCMC) C2C12 cell‐laden bioink with mechanically spun fibers using touch spinning method. The fibrous component provided structural stability to the hybrid 3D construct, enabling high‐density cell (bio) printing without the need for conventional bioink crosslinking. Using fibers with distinct mechanical properties, we reveal that hybrid construct stiffness regulates C2C12 mouse myoblasts skeletal muscle cell behavior. In which stiff, crystalline P3HB fibers induce significantly higher alignment and elongation of C2C12 cells, including both cell bodies and nuclei, compared to the more compliant PCL fibers.

papers.title: Soft-Tissue Phenotype and Long-Term Implant Outcomes: Biological Significance, Clinical Implications, and Management Strategies
papers.abstract: Background: Long-term success in implant dentistry depends not only on osseointegration and implant survival but also on the maintenance of healthy, stable, and esthetically acceptable peri-implant tissues. Increasing attention has therefore been directed toward the peri-implant soft-tissue phenotype, which includes mucosal thickness, keratinized mucosa width, and supracrestal tissue height. Variations in these characteristics may influence marginal bone remodeling, mucosal recession, plaque control, peri-implant inflammation, esthetic stability, and patient comfort.Methods: A structured narrative review of contemporary literature was undertaken with emphasis on consensus reports, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized and controlled clinical trials, prospective studies, and clinically relevant long-term investigations addressing peri-implant mucosal thickness, keratinized mucosa, supracrestal tissue dimensions, soft-tissue augmentation, implant positioning, prosthetic design, marginal bone stability, peri-implant diseases, and esthetic outcomes.Results: Current evidence indicates that thin peri-implant mucosa is associated with greater early marginal bone remodeling and increased susceptibility to soft-tissue dehiscence and recession, although long-term causality remains incompletely established. A limited width of keratinized mucosa does not inevitably lead to peri-implant disease; however, it has been associated with increased plaque accumulation, mucosal recession, inflammatory indices, brushing discomfort, and, in some analyses, greater marginal bone loss. Soft-tissue augmentation can predictably increase mucosal thickness and keratinized mucosa. Autogenous connective tissue grafting generally provides the largest increase in tissue thickness, whereas collagen-based substitutes reduce donor-site morbidity at the cost of somewhat smaller dimensional gains. Implant positioning, facial bone availability, emergence profile, abutment characteristics, maintenance, history of periodontitis, and patient-related factors interact with the soft-tissue phenotype and may be equally or more important than any isolated tissue parameter.Conclusions: Peri-implant soft-tissue phenotype should be regarded as a clinically relevant modifier of biological and esthetic implant outcomes rather than an independent determinant of implant survival. Thin mucosa and limited keratinized tissue deserve particular consideration in esthetically demanding sites and in patients with additional risk factors. Phenotype modification should be based on individualized risk assessment rather than performed routinely around every implant. Long-term, standardized clinical studies are required to define clinically meaningful thresholds and identify patients most likely to benefit from soft tissue augmentation.

papers.title: Cuttlebone-inspired S -lamellar Ti/Mg interpenetrating-phase composites via direct ink writing and pressureless infiltration
papers.abstract: Ti alloys suffer modulus mismatch and poor osseointegration, while Mg alloys have low strength and rapid degradation. Inspired by cuttlebone’s wavy-wall lamellar structure, we developed S-lamellar Ti/Mg interpenetrating-phase composites. Porous Ti scaffolds with structural angles of 90°, 120°, and 150° were fabricated by direct ink writing and pressureless infiltrated with pure Mg, forming a bicontinuous architecture. Compression, bending, and fracture were examined for structural-angle and loading-direction effects. Compressive strengths reached 151–363 MPa and flexural strengths 285–483 MPa, 1.5–2.5 times those of pure Mg and matching human cortical bone. Properties showed coupled anisotropy: under compression, the 120° structure had the highest strength (363 MPa) in XOY; under bending, the 150° structure has the highest strength (483 MPa) in YOZ and the highest apparent fracture toughness in XOY. Fractography revealed that S-shaped zigzag interfaces activated toughening mechanisms including crack deflection, interfacial sliding, and Mg plastic energy dissipation, depending on crack alignment. After 42 h in simulated body fluid, Mg corroded preferentially, with morphology varying by angle; the 90° structure exhibited the greatest strength loss owing to interconnected interfacial corrosion channels. This strategy supports bioinspired design of degradable load-bearing bone implants with combined control of degradation and mechanical performance.

papers.title: Fusion of dual-view hyperspectral imaging with a novel MTBCNN-KDE framework: Reliable quantification of multiple quality markers in cultivated chrysanthemum
papers.abstract: Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat. (Gongju) is a cultivated medicinal and aromatic industrial crop, whose industrial quality is determined by multiple chemical marker compounds relevant to processing and standardization. This study proposes a novel approach integrating dual-view hyperspectral imaging (HSI), a Bayesian-optimized multi-task deep learning framework (MTBCNN), and a kernel density estimation (KDE)–based interval prediction strategy for the simultaneous, non-destructive quantification of four key quality markers. A total of 660 cultivated samples from 11 production regions were analyzed using spectra acquired from two orientations: corolla-upward (A) and receptacle-upward (B). Bayesian optimization enabled automatic hyperparameter tuning, and multi-task models outperformed single-task approaches. The MTBCNN with fused AB data achieved the best results, with all markers reaching R p ² values above 0.82 and RPD values over 2.31. KDE-based interval prediction achieved coverage probabilities of 0.92–0.97, showing stable model performance. Overall, the MTBCNN-KDE framework integrated with HSI provides a scalable and repeatable solution for intelligent quality control of cultivated chrysanthemum, demonstrating strong potential for application in industrial processing and quality standardization along plant-based industrial value chains.

papers.title: Optimized modeling and control of a photovoltaic-thermal collector field for improved thermal comfort and energy efficiency
papers.abstract: Photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) collectors generate electricity and useful heat, requiring a balance between electrical efficiency and thermal recovery. This study proposes a PVT-Building Digital Twin (PVT-BDT) coupled with Adaptive Pareto Model Predictive Control (AP-MPC) to optimize PVT flow rate, HVAC setpoint, and battery/grid power allocation. A 4C-RC electro-thermal model integrates PVT dynamics, building thermal behaviour, occupant comfort, battery state of charge, and electrical power balance. AP-MPC adapts objective weights using the knee point of a periodically approximated energy–comfort Pareto front. The framework is evaluated through calibrated numerical simulations using experimental PVT parameters and data from the Northern African Industrial Thermal Comfort Dataset (NAITCD). Over six months, AP-MPC reduces net energy consumption by 26% compared with fixed-flow control, increases thermal satisfaction from 76.2% to 90.5%, and improves PVT electrical efficiency by 2–7%. These results demonstrate the potential of adaptive Pareto control for energy-efficient, occupant-centered buildings.

papers.title: Analysis and Critical Review of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Twin Approaches for Predictive Maintenance in High-Voltage Substations
papers.abstract: Maintenance of primary equipment in high-voltage substations evolves from time-based routines toward predictive and prescriptive strategies supported by artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twins (DTs). This review traces the evolution of maintenance strategies from corrective to risk-based asset management, summarizes degradation mechanisms, diagnostic indicators and monitoring practice, and identifies the main challenges: aging fleets, new operating stresses, the phase-out of sulfur hexafluoride, and incomplete and imbalanced data. AI models achieve high diagnostic accuracy but are mostly validated on laboratory or single-utility data and rarely quantify uncertainty. Most DT implementations reported to date are digital models or digital shadows, with thermal DTs of power transformers being the most mature, as they rely on standardized thermal models and field data. Particular emphasis is put on prescriptive maintenance, which turns predictions into recommended actions; substation criticality analysis and risk-based and cost-optimal scheduling are discussed, and the first prescriptive frameworks are reviewed. Based on these findings, a conceptual framework and a research roadmap for predictive and prescriptive maintenance are proposed.

papers.title: Room‐Temperature Ferromagnetism and Optical Properties of Hydrothermally Synthesized Co‐Doped β ‐Ga 2 O 3: Experiments and First‐Principles Calculations
papers.abstract: Gallium oxide (Ga 2 O 3) is an ultrawide‐bandgap oxide semiconductor with intrinsic diamagnetism, and cobalt doping provides an effective strategy for introducing localized 3d magnetic moments and regulating its room‐temperature magnetic behavior. In this work, pure and Co‐doped β ‐Ga 2 O 3 powders with different cobalt contents were synthesized by a hydrothermal method followed by calcination, and their structural, morphological, optical, and magnetic properties were investigated in combination with first‐principles calculations based on density functional theory. The experimental results show that all samples retain the monoclinic β ‐Ga 2 O 3 phase without detectable crystalline secondary phases; cobalt incorporation modifies the lattice structure, influences the size distribution and morphology evolution of rod‐like particles, enhances visible‐light absorption, and slightly modifies the optical bandgap. More importantly, cobalt doping transforms β ‐Ga 2 O 3 from a diamagnetic material into a weak ferromagnetic/mixed ferromagnetic–paramagnetic system at room temperature, which may originate from Co‐3d‐derived impurity states, spin polarization, and Co‐3d/O‐2p hybridization.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Abstention for Small Language Models: A Review with an Empirical Case Study on Domain-Specific Question Answering
papers.abstract: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly deployed on devices and in domain-specific settings where a wrong answer is costly, so they need to know when not to answer. Existing surveys of uncertainty quantification (UQ) and abstention focus on large general-purpose models. This paper reviews UQ methods and abstention mechanisms from the perspective of SLM deployment and summarizes evidence that small models tend to be overconfident. We complement the review with a case study on medical multiple-choice questions using three 4B-class models. Conformal prediction meets its coverage target when calibration and test data match, but at a 90% target the models abstain on more than half of the questions, and coverage drops when the calibration data come from a different subject or question source. Calibrating separately for each subject corrects the under-coverage of harder subjects but needs several hundred labeled examples per subject to be reliable. We conclude with open problems for reliable abstention in small models.

papers.title: First years teaching first years: Medical student perspectives of the benefits and challenges of participating in a prosection‐based reciprocal peer‐taught gross anatomy course
papers.abstract: The anatomy laboratory serves as an excellent paradigm for exploring the peer teaching model, especially amid reduced instructional hours and a shortage of qualified educators. While peer teaching is well established in the literature, medical students' perspectives of reciprocal peer teaching in a prosection-based anatomy course remain underexplored. This basic qualitative study explored student perceptions of the benefits and challenges associated with prosection-based reciprocal peer teaching in a gross anatomy laboratory. Four focus groups involving 16 first- and second-year medical students were conducted to reflect the interactive nature of the experience. Thematic analysis was performed using inductive coding to identify themes and subthemes. Rigor was enhanced through thick description, audit trails, and member checks. Four themes were identified from the data: learning by teaching, camaraderie, teaching reliability, and time management. Medical students highlighted their in-depth knowledge of the anatomical content they taught as one of the key benefits of peer teaching, along with the chance to build connections with their peers. Some of the challenges described by the students included a fear of giving or receiving wrong information, inconsistencies in teaching approaches, and finding time to prepare to teach amidst busy medical school schedules. First-year medical students teaching other first-year medical students was generally viewed as a positive experience by the participants, despite noted challenges. This study is a step toward understanding more about how to help medical students learn anatomy through active learning, while also gaining practice in collaboration and conveying information to others.

papers.title: Thermal‐Oxidative Aging Behavior and Storage Life Prediction of MoS 2 / PTFE Composites
papers.abstract: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)‐based composites have been widely used in the aerospace industry due to their excellent chemical stability and self‐lubricating properties. Ensuring the safety, reliability, and maneuverability of high‐end equipment requires a critical assessment of the storage life of materials. In this study, a low‐friction MoS 2 /PTFE composite was taken as the research object. Thermal‐oxidative aging accelerated tests were conducted to systematically investigate its performance evolution at 190°C, 220°C, and 245°C. By analyzing the changes in chemical structure, thermal stability, surface morphology, and tribological performance, it was found that thermal‐oxidative aging destroys the helical twisted chain structure of PTFE and causes a red shift of its characteristic absorption peaks. Meanwhile, chain scission of the macromolecules generates volatile low‐molecular‐weight fragments, and MoS 2 also undergoes oxidation; these two effects jointly promote the formation of a porous structure on the material surface. In this study, the friction coefficient was used as the failure criterion, and a storage life prediction model was constructed based on a physics‐informed neural network (PINN). This model can be used to evaluate the storage life of MoS 2 /PTFE composites, providing a basis for the safe operation and reliable service of high‐end equipment.

papers.title: Nationwide mapping of mangrove EWT and LMA in China using universal sensitive subdomains and Bayesian-optimized machine learning models
papers.abstract: Mangroves support global carbon cycling and biodiversity. Leaf equivalent water thickness (EWT) and leaf mass per area (LMA), core functional traits, are vital ecological monitoring indicators. Yet vague spectral response mechanisms hamper precise, stable large-scale remote sensing inversion. This study constructed a national sensitive spectral screening framework based on 1023 plots and 102,300 full-spectrum field data across China’s mangrove zones. Combining spectral clustering and cross-regional meta-analysis, we used group-differential gradient perturbation two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (GDGP-2D-COS) and Bayesian optimization to extract sensitive bands and identify regional optimal wavelengths and universal sensitive subdomains. We further developed 120 inversion strategies to generate high-resolution national maps of mangrove EWT and LMA across China. Our results reveal universal sensitive subdomains cover 795–878 nm, 968–975 nm, 1735–1765 nm, and 2021–2050 nm; LMA lies in the red edge and SWIR regions: 729–765 nm, 1564–1672 nm, and 1978–1990 nm. Four machine-learning verifications prove that regional and universal bands yield robust accuracy: EWT R 2 = 0.620–0.965, LMA R 2 = 0.504–0.908. Tested on Sentinel-2 and ZY-1 02E data, universal sensitive spectral subdomains remain steady (EWT R 2 = 0.506–0.965; LMA R 2 = 0.444–0.848). China’s mangrove EWT is 0.205–0.550 kg/m2 and LMA 0.06–0.214 kg/m2, matching ecological benchmarks. This work supplies scientific and technical support for mangrove carbon sink assessment, targeted ecosystem management and sustainable conservation.

papers.title: Evolutionary Crosslinking‐Driven 3D Printing of Silicone Elastomers
papers.abstract: Flexible functional systems require materials that combine mechanical compliance, structural stability, and long-term reliability. Silicone elastomers satisfy these requirements through their low modulus, large recoverable deformation, environmental stability, and chemically crosslinked networks. Among them, platinum-catalyzed addition-cure silicones are particularly attractive because of their low curing shrinkage, uniform networks, and stable properties. However, increasing structural complexity and functional integration challenge conventional mold-based fabrication and motivate additive manufacturing of complex silicone architectures. A central challenge in silicone 3D printing is to move beyond tailoring materials for printability toward designing printing processes around their intrinsic material behavior, thereby enabling precise control over both geometry and properties. Unlike thermoplastics or photocurable elastomers, addition-cure silicones undergo continuous, time- and temperature-dependent crosslinking after mixing, leading to concurrent evolution of crosslinking state, rheology, and mechanical stability during shaping. This Review defines this process as evolutionary crosslinking and introduces "crosslinking-in-shaping" to describe manufacturing in which structure generation is intrinsically coupled with crosslinking evolution. This Review establishes a five-step framework for extrusion-based silicone additive manufacturing, reorganizing existing studies from a manufacturing-science perspective. The framework is also applicable to other thermosetting material systems governed by irreversible crosslinking and thermal regulation.

papers.title: Weather-Aware Neuro-Fuzzy Model Predictive Control for Outdoor Microalgae Raceways
papers.abstract: Outdoor microalgae raceways require pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) regulation under variable weather and bounded gas actuation. The proposed method combines a regularized multioutput adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system with model predictive control (MPC). Rule weights are recomputed every minute and held constant over a 60 min prediction horizon, preserving convexity of the optimization. Four controllers were compared in 288 benchmark simulations spanning twelve synthetic weather realizations, three forecast modes and two conditioning profiles. Relative to linear MPC, the proposed controller reduced the mean common control cost by 9.22% (conditional 95% weather-group bootstrap interval: 8.22–10.26%), pH root-mean-square error by 14.75%, and accumulated DO excess by 34.00%. Commanded carbon dioxide and air volumes increased by 0.56% and 1.32%, respectively. These results quantify the trade-off between regulation and commanded gas use in the scenarios tested. The control score does not measure cultivation productivity or economic return.

papers.title: Prestabilized Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Robust Trajectory Tracking and Tension Regulation in Tethered UAVs
papers.abstract: This paper presents a prestabilized nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) design approach to achieve trajectory tracking and tether tension regulation for a tethered unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) subject to disturbances. The tethered UAV dynamics are expressed in an affine‐in‐input form with respect to the thrust magnitude and winch torque, and then a baseline prestabilizing controller is derived to regulate tether coordinates, for which local asymptotic tracking stability is established through the Lyapunov stability theorem. Building on this nominal stabilizing action, an NMPC law is designed to optimize tracking performance while explicitly handling state and input constraints and simultaneously controlling the vehicle attitude. The proposed architecture is motivated by the observation that pure (nominal) NMPC may not perform well or be robust at lower prediction horizons, which are preferred to reduce online computational burden. Simulation studies under time‐varying disturbances show that the proposed prestabilized NMPC maintains closed‐loop stability at short prediction horizons and demonstrates improved robust tracking performance and feasibility over baseline NMPC.

papers.title: Cognitive Digital Twin Integration in Adaptive Mechatronic Systems: A Self-Optimizing Architecture for Industry 5.0
papers.abstract: In this study, we propose a Cognitive Digital Twin (CDT) architecture for adaptive mechatronic systems under the Industry 5.0 paradigm is proposed in this paper: the Cognitive Digital Twin (CDT) architecture.The architecture integrates physics-based simulation models with real-time machine learning inference to facilitate self-optimizing actions at the sensing, actuating, and human-in-the-loop control levels.We explain a five-layer architecture (physical, digital replica, cognitive inference, adaptive control, and human interaction), a reinforcement-learning-based adaptive control policy designed within formally defined safety envelopes, and a calibrated uncertainty-quantification pipeline for a safe fallback behaviour.We provide a complete hardware-in-theloop validation protocol, including metrics for the baseline, primary, and secondary metrics, as well as a pre-registered statistical analysis plan, to validate the complete architecture on a six-degree-of-freedom collaborative robotic assembly cell, which has not been performed yet.As initial evidence for the core adaptation mechanism, we report the results of a softwarein-the-loop simulation, which were repeatable over 30 paired episodes, with an online-adaptive controller outperforming three progressively more sophisticated non-adaptive baseline controllers in terms of reduced settling time (by 14.4%, all p < 0.001, Cohen's d 0.83-3.36)and reduced downtime (by 11.0%, all p < 0.001, Cohen's d 0.83-3.36)under randomized plant non-stationarity, but at the same time increasing control energy by 32-85% (a genuine and honest trade-off, not a rule of thumb) relative to the strongest baseline.The architecture is hardware-independent and can be expanded to other cyberphysical systems, such as smart manufacturing, medical robotics, and precision agriculture.
